item.title: Living in Fenegrò and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide on taxation, connections and costs for those who choose Fenegrò as a residence working in the Canton of Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Imposta alla fonte trattenuta solo in Svizzera - Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024 - Franchigia di 10.000 euro per i nuovi frontalieri - Esenzione di 7.500 euro per i vecchi frontalieri (fino al 2033)
## Fatti chiave Accordo Frontalieri: firmato 23/12/2020, vigente dal 01/01/2024 Ratifica Italia: Legge 83 del 13/06/2023 Convenzione doppie imposizioni: 09/12/1976 Franchigia nuovi frontalieri: 10.000 € Esenzione vecchi frontalieri: 7.500 € Trattenuta fiscale: Solo in Svizzera
La scelta di risiedere a Fenegrò per lavorare nel Canton Ticino si inserisce in un quadro normativo preciso, regolato principalmente dal Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri firmato il 23 dicembre 2020 e in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024. Tale accordo, ratificato in Italia con la Legge 83 del 13 giugno 2023, definisce i parametri fiscali per chi attraversa il confine quotidianamente. La Svizzera, pur non essendo membro UE/SEE, mantiene rapporti stabili con l'Italia basati anche sulla Convenzione per evitare le doppie imposizioni firmata il 9 dicembre 1976.
### Il regime fiscale applicato Per chi lavora in Ticino e risiede a Fenegrò, l'imposta alla fonte sul reddito da lavoro viene trattenuta esclusivamente in Svizzera. L'Italia evita la doppia imposizione attraverso l'applicazione di un credito d'imposta, che il contribuente deve indicare nel quadro CE della dichiarazione dei redditi (modello 730). Questo meccanismo assicura che il carico fiscale sia gestito correttamente tra i due Stati, senza che il lavoratore paghi l'imposta intera in entrambi i paesi.
La gestione delle aliquote fiscali, sia a livello federale che cantonale, è affidata all'Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni (AFC/ESTV) e alle rispettive amministrazioni cantonali. È importante sottolineare che enti come l'Ufficio Federale di Statistica (BFS) o l'UFAS si occupano rispettivamente di rilevazioni dati e previdenza sociale, e non hanno alcun potere nella fissazione delle aliquote fiscali. Per chi desidera analizzare l'impatto di queste trattenute sul proprio stipendio, è possibile utilizzare un [calcolatore](nav:calculator) per stimare il netto mensile. L'analisi della convenienza di vivere a Fenegrò comporta la valutazione di diversi scenari fiscali a seconda della data di inizio dell'attività di frontaliere. Il sistema attuale distingue nettamente tra chi era già frontaliere prima del 17 luglio 2023 e chi ha iniziato successivamente.
### Differenze tra nuovi e vecchi frontalieri I cosiddetti vecchi frontalieri beneficiano di un regime transitorio che copre il periodo 2024–2033, mantenendo un'esenzione fiscale di 7.500 euro. Al contrario, i nuovi frontalieri, ovvero coloro che hanno acquisito lo status dopo la data limite, possono beneficiare di una franchigia di 10.000 euro. Questa distinzione è fondamentale per il calcolo del reddito imponibile in Italia e per l'eventuale determinazione del credito d'imposta.
Dal punto di vista dei contributi sociali, il sistema svizzero prevede trattenute precise che incidono sulla busta paga. I contributi AVS/AI/IPG sono fissati al 5,3% a carico del dipendente, mentre l'assicurazione disoccupazione (AD/AC) assorbe l'1,1%, con un tetto massimo di 148.200 CHF. A questi si aggiunge la LAINF, che varia tra lo 0,7% e l'1,5%, e la previdenza professionale LPP, con aliquote che oscillano tra il 7% e il 18% a seconda della fascia d'età, a partire dai 25 anni.
### Il costo della vita e l'assicurazione sanitaria Risiedere in Italia e lavorare in Svizzera permette di ottimizzare il costo della vita, ma introduce l'obbligo di gestire l'assicurazione malattia (LAMal). I frontalieri con permesso G hanno un diritto d'opzione che permette di scegliere tra il sistema svizzero e quello del paese di residenza. Nel caso in cui si scelga la LAMal, le franchigie per gli adulti variano da 300 a 2.500 CHF. Per confrontare l'incidenza di queste spese rispetto al salario svizzero, si consiglia di consultare i dati sul [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) tra Ticino e Italia. Per chi decide di trasferirsi a Fenegrò e iniziare a lavorare in Ticino, è necessario seguire una procedura amministrativa rigorosa per regolarizzare la propria posizione fiscale e previdenziale.
### Step operativi per il frontaliere Il primo passo consiste nell'ottenere il permesso G, il documento che attesta la qualità di lavoratore transfrontaliero. Una volta iniziato l'impiego, il datore di lavoro provvederà alla trattenuta dell'imposta alla fonte, che verrà versata alle autorità fiscali svizzere. Parallelamente, il lavoratore deve monitorare i propri contributi versati all'AVS e alla LPP per la futura pensione.
In Italia, l'Agenzia delle Entrate e il MEF gestiscono la ricezione dei redditi prodotti all'estero. È essenziale che il frontaliere presenti correttamente la dichiarazione dei redditi, utilizzando il quadro CE del modello 730 per richiedere il credito d'imposta e neutralizzare la doppia imposizione, come previsto dalla Convenzione del 1976. Per chi ha dubbi sulla compilazione o sugli importi, è possibile utilizzare un simulatore per la [dichiarazione redditi](nav:tax-return).
### Gestione delle scadenze e degli enti È fondamentale tenere traccia delle comunicazioni provenienti da AFC/ESTV per quanto riguarda le tasse e dall'INPS per l'eventuale coordinamento previdenziale. Se si opta per l'assicurazione sanitaria svizzera, occorre definire la franchigia LAMal entro i termini previsti per evitare sanzioni o coperture limitate.
Per chi è ancora in fase di valutazione del trasferimento, l'analisi del salario lordo rispetto alle trattenute previdenziali e fiscali è il punto di partenza. Calcolare con precisione quanto rimarrà in tasca dopo l'imposta alla fonte e i contributi LPP è l'unico modo per pianificare correttamente il budget familiare a Fenegrò. Per ottenere una stima accurata, suggeriamo di utilizzare il nostro [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: Living in Cantù and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide for those who choose Cantù as their residence: taxation, new border agreement, AVS, LAMal and management of daily commuting to Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Agreement entered into force on January 1, 2024. - Exclusive taxation in Switzerland with a tax credit in Italy. - 10,000 euro tax allowance for new cross-border workers. - Mandatory LAMal insurance for employees with a G permit.
## Key facts Cross-border Workers Agreement: December 23, 2020 Entry into force: January 1, 2024 Allowance for new cross-border workers: 10,000 euro Allowance for existing cross-border workers: 7,500 euro AVS/AI/IPG contribution: 5.3% employee share AD/AC contribution: 1.1% (cap 148,200 CHF)
Moving to Cantù for those working in the Canton of Ticino is a choice that requires careful planning, based on the current regulations governing the relationship between Italy and Switzerland. Since January 1, 2024, the new agreement signed on December 23, 2020, has introduced substantial changes for cross-border workers. Income from employment is taxed exclusively in Switzerland via withholding tax, managed by the cantonal tax administrations and the Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV). To avoid double taxation, the worker must declare the income in Italy, utilizing the tax credit through the CE section of the 730 tax return form.
### Updated tax regulations Workers who were already cross-border commuters before July 17, 2023, benefit from a transitional regime valid until 2033, with a tax exemption of 7,500 euro. For those hired after that date, the allowance is set at 10,000 euro. It is essential to remember that Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member; therefore, the relationship is regulated by the Convention for the avoidance of double taxation signed on December 9, 1976. Swiss social security contributions, such as AVS, AI, and IPG, amount to 5.3% charged to the employee, while unemployment insurance (AD/AC) is 1.1% up to a salary cap of 148,200 francs. The management of these contributions is the responsibility of social security institutions, while tax rates are established by federal and cantonal laws. A cross-border worker residing in Cantù must carefully consider these payroll deductions, which differ significantly from the Italian tax system. Financial planning must also integrate the impact of Italian IRPEF, with brackets at 23%, 35%, and 43% based on total income, applied net of the tax credit recognized for taxes already paid across the border. ### Practical implications of commuting Choosing Cantù means dealing daily with the dynamics of cross-border traffic towards the Canton of Ticino. The main road connection involves using the A9 motorway network, which merges towards the Brogeda border crossing, a nerve center for access into Swiss territory. Managing travel time is a critical factor for those residing far from the immediate border. It is advisable to constantly monitor traffic conditions, as unforeseen events or congestion peaks can heavily influence the quality of work life. From a social security perspective, in addition to the mandatory AVS contributions, the worker must assess their position regarding the second pillar (LPP), with rates varying between 7% and 18% based on age, starting from 25 years old. Managing health insurance coverage is equally crucial: cross-border workers holding a G permit have the right of option for LAMal, the mandatory Swiss health insurance, which provides for deductibles between 300 and 2,500 francs. It is essential not to confuse LAMal with a tax, as it is an insurance coverage necessary to access healthcare services. Compared to the past, the regulatory framework requires greater awareness of income tax declaration procedures. The taxpayer must ensure they correctly document every payment made in Switzerland to maximize the benefit of the tax credit in Italy, thus avoiding excessive taxation. The distinction between withholding tax, managed by the FTA, and social contributions managed by social security institutions, must be clear for every worker. Proper maintenance of tax documentation, keeping copies of Swiss payslips and salary certificates, is the first step for a smooth management of one's status as a cross-border worker residing in Cantù. Family budget planning must include not only transport costs but also currency exchange fluctuations, considering that income is received in Swiss francs.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Operational procedures and useful tools For those intending to settle in Cantù and embark on a career path in Ticino, the procedure begins with obtaining the G permit, issued by the competent authorities following a regular employment contract. Subsequently, it is necessary to regularize one's insurance status. The worker must activate LAMal coverage or exercise the right of option, depending on their specific situation, to ensure compliance with current regulations. Regarding social security, it is advisable to monitor one's AVS position and evaluate joining supplementary pension schemes, such as the third pillar, to supplement future income. Managing income requires the use of digital tools to simulate the net salary, considering tax deductions and Swiss social contributions. To effectively compare net income, it is useful to use a [tax calculator](nav:calculator) that allows for estimating the impact of withholding tax and the Italian tax credit. Furthermore, financial planning must take into account commuting costs, including car maintenance expenses and the potential purchase of the Swiss motorway vignette, which is necessary for traveling on Swiss highways. For those wishing to optimize the exchange rate management between CHF and EUR, constant monitoring of exchange rates through a [currency comparator](nav:exchange) is a recommended practice. Finally, for those needing to delve into their health coverage, a [health insurance comparator](nav:health) is available to evaluate the various options offered by LAMal. Transparency and constant updates are the keys to managing one's status as a cross-border worker autonomously and in an informed manner. Any change in income or family situation must be promptly communicated to the competent tax authorities, both in Switzerland and in Italy, to avoid discrepancies in annual declarations. By using the simulation and planning tools provided, the worker can obtain a clear and realistic view of their net income, facilitating prudent and long-term oriented financial management.

The brief goes out early each morning, before the commute; numbers are a snapshot at publication time, the linked pages stay live all day.

item.title: Health insurance premiums: the PLR proposes a cantonal strategy
item.description: The PLR calls for quarterly monitoring of healthcare costs after the 7.1% increase in premiums recorded in Ticino in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The FDP proposes a cantonal strategy to curb healthcare costs. - In 2026, health insurance premiums in Ticino rose by 7.1%. - Public spending for RIPAM has increased by 47% in six years. - A quarterly monitoring of healthcare costs in Ticino has been requested.
## Key facts Submission date: September 21, 2026 Proponent: Alessandra Gianella Political group: FDP 2026 premium increase Ticino: 7.1% 2026 premium increase Switzerland: 4.4% 2026 adult premium increase: 6.9% 2026 young adult premium increase: 7.3% 2026 minor premium increase: 7.7%
On September 21, 2026, Alessandra Gianella, on behalf of the FDP group, presented a motion to the Grand Council aimed at implementing a cantonal strategy to contain healthcare spending. The initiative stems from the need to intervene structurally in the costs fueling the growth of health insurance premiums, moving beyond the simple provision of subsidies. The context highlighted by the text is that of a Ticino which recorded an average premium increase of 7.1% in 2026, a figure higher than the 4.4% recorded at the national level. Analyzing the progression by age group, the motion underlines how for adults the increase was 6.9%, for young adults 7.3%, and for minors 7.7%. The projections by bonus.ch mentioned in the document also indicate the possibility of a further national price hike of between 4.5% and 5% for 2027.
### The impact on public coffers The motion emphasizes the financial sustainability of the system, highlighting how the overall expenditure for the Reduction of health insurance premiums (RIPAM) and the coverage of premiums for beneficiaries of OASI/DI supplementary benefits has risen significantly. Specifically, it went from 307.7 million francs in 2020 to 426 million in 2025, with a forecast of 453.5 million for 2026. This increase, equal to about 47% in just six years, raises questions about the stability of the current model. The FDP believes that politics cannot limit itself to transferring the burden of costs from the insured to the taxpayers, highlighting how the middle class is particularly exposed to this dynamic, suffering a contraction of disposable income due to high premiums and the low incidence of individual reduction measures for this category. The analysis proposed by the FDP focuses on the need for more rigorous and transparent healthcare governance within the Canton of Ticino. The motion calls for the introduction of a quarterly, concise, and accessible monitoring of compulsory insurance costs, based on data already available at the federal level. The goal is to break down expenses by major service groups, comparing them with national averages and those of other comparable cantons. In addition to this control tool, an in-depth annual analysis is proposed to identify the causes of expenditure deviations and the sectors where costs are growing most rapidly. Such data should serve as the basis for a cantonal containment strategy, to be updated at least once per legislative period, which defines priorities, measurable objectives, and concrete measures under cantonal jurisdiction.
### Supply planning and EFAS reform A central element of the proposal concerns the planning of healthcare supply, both stationary and outpatient, with the intent of aligning it with the actual needs of the population. The FDP aims to limit redundant capacities and oversupply, which can generate additional costs without providing concrete health benefits. The EFAS reform on the uniform financing of services fits into this framework. The FDP's request is that the Canton prepares for the implementation of the reform not only from a financial perspective, but by favoring the shift of services from the stationary to the outpatient sector, where clinically appropriate. This would improve the overall efficiency of the supply. Furthermore, the motion proposes the establishment of a structured annual dialogue between the main players in Ticino's healthcare system to formulate concrete containment proposals, clearly distinguishing between interventions under cantonal and federal jurisdiction. Regarding transparency, it is requested that every cantonal health policy decision be accompanied by an indication of the expected impact on compulsory insurance costs and that the Government submit a biennial report to the Grand Council on the evolution of expenditure and the results achieved.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). For citizens and workers residing or active in Ticino, the issue of rising LAMal premiums represents a primary expense. The FDP motion directly impacts household budgets, which face constant increases and growing indirect fiscal pressure. It is crucial to understand that while the political debate focuses on cost-containment strategies, individual policyholders must continue to actively manage their insurance status. The transparency requested by the motion, if translated into public reports and accessible monitoring, will allow for a clearer view of the factors influencing healthcare spending, facilitating more informed choices. For those working in Ticino, it is essential to constantly monitor price dynamics and available coverage.
### Tools for cost management While waiting for healthcare cost-containment strategies to be implemented, policyholders can utilize established tools to manage their budgets. Choosing the right deductible and regularly reviewing contractual conditions remain the pillars for optimizing the impact of premiums on net income. It is advisable to use official comparison tools to evaluate the various options offered by health insurance funds, keeping in mind that the LAMal system guarantees mandatory coverage but allows for personalized management of risk levels and monthly premiums. For those wishing to delve deeper into the impact of healthcare spending and social charges on their salary, it is essential to use accurate calculation tools. Managing one's payslip, also considering AVS contributions and tax withholdings, requires a clear overview. To verify how different salary components and deductions affect your monthly net income and to better plan the management of your earnings, we invite you to use the [calculator](nav:calculator) dedicated to payslips and taxes.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/politica/1951514/premi-di-cassa-malati-il-plr-intervenire-sui-costi-della-sanita)*

item.title: Recruitment in the public sector in Ticino: clear rules requested
item.description: Roncelli and Mirante di Avanti with Ticino & Lavoro ask the government about the Zali case and the 2020 email to the ECO.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Question by Roncelli and Mirante to the government - Request for clarification on the Zali case and the 2020 email - Focus on EoC recruitment and transparency
## Key facts - Applicants: Roncelli and Mirante (Forward with Ticino & Lavoro) - Episode: Zali case and 2020 email - Entity involved: EOC - Request: Provisions to prevent similar situations
Clear rules are needed to ensure transparency and impartiality in recruitment. This is the central theme raised in the Canton of Ticino by the political representatives Roncelli and Mirante of the Avanti con Ticino & Lavoro movement. The political leaders decided to submit a formal question to the cantonal government to shed light on specific events that have attracted public and institutional attention.
At the centre of the request is the so-called Zali case and a specific email communication dating back to 2020 addressed to the ECO, the Cantonal Hospital Authority. The question aims to understand in detail how the dynamics took place on thatoccasion and what are the administrative implications related to the selection and appointment procedures within the bodies governed by public law or participated in by the Canton.
### The request for institutional clarifications The initiative of the two members of Avanti con Ticino & Lavoro is not limited to retracing the events of the past, but looks directly at the future of cantonal administrative and health management. The issue raised in the public debate closely touches on the delicate balance between political management and the administration of public entities in Ticino Canton. When discussing healthcare institutions such as the EOC, whose strategic importance for the resident and cross-border population and workforce is central, any doubt about the regularity of recruitment processes risks undermining general trust in institutions. The demand for clear, unambiguous guidelines aims precisely to secure procedures, excluding any margin of discretion not strictly regulated by law.
Within selective procedures, the adoption of rigorous standards ensures candidates are evaluated exclusively on the basis of professional competencies—a fundamental aspect for protecting merit and the quality of services provided. The interrogators stress the need for regulatory intervention or binding directives to act as a shield against any decision-making opacity, offering guarantees to both internal staff and external participants in public competitions.
### The impact on the governance of public entities The response from the Ticino government to the inquiry by Roncelli and Mirante will likely outline the scope of future control actions on competitions and appointments within the Ente Ospedaliero Cantonale (EOC) and other public structures in the territory. For workers and citizens, administrative transparency represents a key indicator of the democratic quality of cantonal management. Political discussion thus shifts toward the need to modernize and make decision-making processes governing access to key roles in Ticino's public administration immune to conflicts of interest.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). To gain a deeper understanding of the administrative situation and stay updated on regulatory developments concerning the labor market and the management of public entities in the Canton of Ticino, it is advisable to regularly consult official sources and news published by local media outlets. The institutional dynamics related to the transparency of competitions and the decisions of the cantonal government provide ongoing insights for understanding the evolution of hiring rules in the public and healthcare sectors.
The procedure initiated through the parliamentary inquiry represents one of the oversight tools available to political representatives to stimulate dialogue with the executive and obtain transparent responses on past and future events. Citizens and industry professionals can monitor the process of government responses through the institutional channels of the Ticinese Grand Council, where issues concerning the management of public affairs and oversight of entities subsidized or dependent on the Canton are filed and discussed.
### Verification of Tools and Resources For those who wish to thoroughly analyze their employment status, tax data, or economic conditions within the Ticinese context, online simulation and calculation tools are available. To obtain a precise assessment of taxes and net remuneration from your employment, you can immediately access the [tax calculator](nav:calculator) to quickly and intuitively estimate salary, taxes, and deductions.

## In brief - Statement by an Fdi parliamentarian - A fund to provide better pay - Workers in the border region - Staying to work in Italy
## Key facts Who: Fdi parliamentarian Target audience: Border region workers Objective: Better remuneration in Italy
The political and institutional debate on measures to support employment in border areas has seen a new intervention by a national political figure. A parliamentarian belonging to Fratelli d'Italia recently intervened in the public debate to clarify the purposes of a specific financial instrument aimed at supporting the local economic and labor fabric.
### The allocation of resources The fund in question, according to what was specified by the Fdi parliamentarian, will assume a central role in managing wage and employment dynamics in neighboring territorial areas. The measure described by the political figure is specifically designed to intervene in the economic conditions of personnel employed on national territory.
The issue of enhancing professional skills and economic treatment represents a central theme for Italian border territories, where historically there are dynamics of labor force mobility towards Switzerland. The statements made by the political representative offer an interpretation of the intentions regarding the use of resources allocated for this specific purpose.
The context of the border region Geographical areas bordering Switzerland have long experienced a complex employment reality, characterized by wage differentials that push many workers to consider cross-border jobs. In this scenario, the intervention announced by the Fdi parliamentarian aims to directly impact the opportunities offered by the local Italian labor market.
The discussion surrounding the fund and its operation is part of a broader framework of institutional attention towards local communities and workers who choose to carry out their work activity within national borders, trying to bridge the existing economic gap.
The political figure's stance aims to highlight the importance of supporting resident employment and offering concrete incentives so that the local workforce can find professional and economic prospects in Italian border territories that meet their expectations. The analysis of the statements made by the Fdi parliamentarian allows for an examination of the practical implications connected to the management of the fund designated for the border region. The employment dynamics affecting border areas require targeted interventions to fully understand the impact that similar measures can generate on the local economic fabric.
### Wage dynamics and the labor market The choice to focus on the remuneration of workers who decide to stay and work in Italy responds to a long-felt need in border areas. The comparison between the economic conditions offered by Italian companies and those across the border represents one of the determining factors in the professional choices of residents.
The fund described by the Fdi parliamentarian serves as an operational tool aimed at influencing this dynamic, seeking to offer economic support capable of making employment in the national territory more attractive. However, the evaluation of such measures requires careful observation of the modalities with which resources will actually be distributed and applied in local contexts.
### Prospects for resident workers For workers operating in the Italian border zone, the prospect of wage improvement represents a significant element in planning their professional path. The possibility of counting on adequate economic recognition can positively influence the decision to remain tied to the domestic labor market.
The practical implications of such a provision are reflected not only on individual employees, but also on local companies operating in border areas. The latter often face difficulties in finding and retaining qualified personnel, due to the strong competition exerted by Swiss economic entities.
The analysis of the announced measures highlights the complexity of intervening in a labor market strongly interconnected with the Swiss economy, where every economic support initiative must contend with the real competitiveness needs of businesses and the salary expectations of workers.

The operational translation of the intentions expressed by the FdI parliamentarian requires monitoring the institutional and regulatory steps necessary to make the fund operational. In border areas, economic operators and workers are closely following the evolution of measures intended to impact local wages.

For the workers concerned, understanding the timing and methods of access to resources represents a fundamental aspect to concretely evaluate the opportunities offered.
Local institutions and social partners play a leading role in defining and monitoring procedures, so that the allocated resources can effectively reach the final recipients intended by the measure. Transparency in the allocation criteria constitutes an essential element to guarantee the correct application of the provisions.
### Information and insights To stay constantly updated on news relating to the labor market in border areas and on institutional initiatives affecting workers, it is possible to consult the sections dedicated to employment services on the reference portal for cross-border workers. Access to detailed and verified information makes it possible to best navigate the regulatory and economic changes that characterize the cross-border area.

item.title: Inflation in Switzerland: how much does it weigh on budgets?
item.description: Analysis of inflation and purchasing power in Switzerland: find out the distance between the official index and the cost of living lived every day.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Analysis of inflation and purchasing power in Switzerland - Gap between official inflation and daily experience - The real weight of energy, fuels, and taxes ## Key facts Author: Elio del Biaggio Date: Sep 20, 2026 Update: 19:01
In Switzerland, inflation, price stability, and purchasing power are regularly discussed through figures that, on paper, appear reassuring for citizens and for those who cross the border daily to work in the Canton of Ticino. However, there is a fundamental question that we should have the courage to ask ourselves: whether we are truly measuring everything that heavily impacts family budgets. Between the official inflation reported by statistical indices and the one actually experienced every day at home and on the roads, the gap can prove to be particularly significant. The central core of the issue does not lie in questioning the correctness of the statistics themselves, but rather in understanding what these indicators actually measure and, above all, which fundamental items are deliberately excluded from the reference baskets. When we witness substantial price increases that directly hit primary sectors such as energy, fuels, foodstuffs, housing-related costs, transportation, health insurance premiums, and a wide range of essential services, the cost of daily life grows in a tangible and unmistakable way. ### The hidden pressure on family budgets To the spending on basic necessities are also added taxes, duties, fiscal charges, and further levies that directly or indirectly weigh on final consumer prices, further amplifying the economic pressure on the domestic budgets of residents and cross-border workers. Taking the fuel sector as an example, the price paid at the pump does not depend exclusively on international fluctuations in the cost of oil on global markets, but is largely determined by significant taxation and ancillary charges. Similarly, the cost of energy is not confined to simple car refueling or the domestic electricity bill, but penetrates thoroughly into the price of any good or service that is produced, transported, commercialized, and ultimately purchased and consumed by citizens. Energy is practically present everywhere and inevitably conditions every expense. It is therefore insufficient and misleading to state that overall inflation is contained when, at the same time, a family is forced to allocate an increasingly large share of its income to maintaining the exact same standard of living as before. A purely average index may be impeccable and correct from a strictly statistical point of view, but at the same time prove entirely inadequate and unrepresentative of the actual daily experience lived by a household. Not all consumers purchase the exact same goods, not all face the same structure of fixed and variable costs, and not all suffer with the same intensity from the repercussions of price increases recorded in different economic sectors. For this reason, simply speaking generically about inflation without analyzing the complexity of overall economic pressure can become a misleading exercise that fails to capture the financial reality of taxpayers. ### A statistical snapshot that does not match reality The concrete risk associated with this approach is the construction of a representation of reality that appears artificially reassuring, while the management of everyday household budgets tells a completely different story characterized by greater financial difficulties. An official inflation rate maintained at low levels can easily turn into an untruthful figure when evaluated against the overall perception of the cost of living, especially where all the expense items that heavily impact the economic stability of families are not adequately included and weighted. Addressing this issue requires an approach based on realism and, above all, the utmost intellectual honesty, avoiding sugarcoating an economic situation in which real costs constantly exceed the official estimates published by federal statistical agencies.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). Carefully assessing the real impact of inflation on your household budget requires adopting adequate financial planning tools, capable of monitoring the evolution of mandatory and discretionary expenses month after month. For frontier workers and for those who manage entries and exits between Swiss francs and euros, constantly comparing their spending capacity with the real data of the Ticino market is a fundamental measure to avoid unwanted surprises at the end of the year. It is possible to deepen the management of your personal finances, estimate the impact of deductions and verify your economic situation using the [calcolatore](nav:calculator) to better plan the available resources and deal with the cost of living increases with greater awareness.

item.title: Confapi Varese-AVSI agreement for youth training
item.description: Protocol signed on 17 September between Confapi Varese and the AVSI Foundation to train young people through apprenticeships and dual training.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Signed protocol between Confapi Varese and Fondazione AVSI - Objective: train young people through apprenticeship and dual training - Signing took place on September 17 at the Lodovico Pogliaghi House Museum
## Key facts - Signing entity: Confapi Varese - Signing entity: Fondazione AVSI - Signing date: September 17 - Location: Lodovico Pogliaghi House Museum - Parties involved: Marco Tenaglia, Giorgio Capitanio, Roberto Di Francesco
On September 17, in the evocative setting of the Lodovico Pogliaghi House Museum in Santa Maria del Monte, a new memorandum of understanding was signed between Confapi Varese and Fondazione AVSI. The event, part of the benefit evening entitled ‘On the Notes of Varese, Rio and the World’, saw the participation of prominent figures from the two organizations, called upon to formalize a joint commitment aimed at creating a bridge between young people in reception pathways and the productive fabric of small and medium-sized enterprises in the Varese area. The evening was further enriched by the artistic performances of soprano Fernanda Schleder and baritone Frederico de Assis, coming from the Rio de Janeiro Opera Theatre, creating a blend of culture and social purpose.
### Strategic objectives of the protocol The signing of the document, affixed by Marco Tenaglia for Confapi Varese and by Giorgio Capitanio, AVSI Europe Regional Manager, marks the formal start of an operational collaboration. The primary intent is to structure a pathway that combines reception, training and job placement. Fondazione AVSI, leveraging the network of Families for Reception that follows young people in their personal development, will be responsible for identifying profiles ready for the labour market. Confapi Varese, for its part, will deploy its services dedicated to apprenticeship, involving the extensive network of associated small and medium-sized industries. The aim is to effectively meet the professional skill needs of companies, while at the same time offering young people a concrete channel to achieve professional autonomy. This synergy aims to turn corporate social responsibility into an established practice, capable of generating measurable benefits both for companies and for the local Varese community. The agreement fits into an economic landscape in which, according to the source, one out of two companies records serious difficulties in finding the professional figures it needs for its productive activities. The initiative is not limited to a mere programmatic intent, but translates into an operational model based on dual training, which facilitates the insertion of young people into the productive system. The involvement of Api Servizi alle Imprese, in the person of its CEO Roberto Di Francesco, guarantees the provision of specific know-how in training and apprenticeship, essential for building tailor-made paths that respond to the real needs of the small and medium-sized enterprises associated with Confapi.
### Integration and value of work The president of Confapi Varese, Marco Tenaglia, stressed that the ultimate goal is to look to the future, laying the foundations for an authentic and structured integration. The outlined path is based on three fundamental pillars: training, welcome, and cultural value. These components, if correctly integrated, are able to produce tangible benefits both for the young people involved and for the country as a whole. The structure of the agreement provides for a clear distinction of operational competencies: AVSI manages the accompaniment and preparation phase of the young people through its widespread network, while Confapi Varese coordinates the technical phase of job insertion. This systemic approach aims to bridge the gap between the demand for technical skills from companies and the training offer, seeking to make the job insertion process a smooth and well-oiled mechanism capable of enhancing the potential of each young participant in the program. Attention to dual training represents, in this sense, the response to a shortage of professional figures that penalizes not only large industries, but especially the small realities that constitute the economic backbone of the Varese territory.

Per le imprese del territorio interessate ad aderire a questo modello di inserimento, il primo passo operativo consiste nel rivolgersi alla struttura tecnica di Confapi Varese, che attraverso i propri servizi dedicati all'apprendistato, coordina le richieste di formazione duale. Le aziende possono richiedere informazioni direttamente al servizio di Api Servizi alle Imprese per comprendere come strutturare percorsi di inserimento che siano in linea con le competenze ricercate e con le finalità del protocollo sottoscritto con AVSI. La collaborazione mira a fornire alle PMI le competenze necessarie per formare internamente i giovani, riducendo il tempo di ricerca del personale e garantendo una crescita professionale monitorata e strutturata secondo le esigenze produttive del comparto industriale di riferimento.
### Come procedere per le aziende Le realtà interessate devono valutare la propria disponibilità ad accogliere giovani in apprendistato, verificando la compatibilità con i programmi di formazione duale previsti dal protocollo. Il processo prevede una fase di analisi delle competenze necessarie in azienda, seguita da un matching con i giovani individuati da Fondazione AVSI. Per le imprese che desiderano approfondire i meccanismi di gestione del personale e delle assunzioni, è possibile consultare i dati relativi al proprio settore di riferimento o esplorare le opportunità di inserimento attraverso i canali ufficiali dell'associazione. Chi fosse interessato a monitorare costantemente le opportunità di networking o le iniziative di formazione nel settore, può far riferimento alle guide e agli strumenti disponibili per orientarsi nel mercato del lavoro, come quelli consultabili tramite il portale [annunci lavoro](nav:jobs). La struttura del protocollo garantisce un accompagnamento continuo, assicurando che l'inserimento non sia solo un momento di assunzione, ma un percorso di crescita che risponda alle sfide di un mercato del lavoro dinamico e sempre più esigente in termini di specializzazione tecnica.

Enrico Barbazza, mayor of Malesco, has formalized an urgent request addressed to the highest offices of the Italian State, including the President of the Council of Ministers, the Minister of Economy and Finance, and the Minister of the Interior, as well as parliamentarians from border regions. The letter aims to raise the issue regarding the defense of financial resources derived from cross-border labor, which are allocated to border municipalities according to current regulations. The mayor of Malesco emphasizes that these funds do not represent a discretionary concession, but rather a resource linked to an economic and social phenomenon that daily impacts thousands of workers and their families. Without the resources derived from cross-border work, municipalities risk being unable to adequately guarantee essential services such as land maintenance, security, road networks, transport, and social services. Mayor Barbazza highlights how the border condition entails specific burdens that local communities have been concretely supporting for years. The concern expressed in the letter regards the risk that any decisions aimed at withholding or reducing these sums could severely penalize the territories involved. item.title: Swiss Border Study: Border Costs and Collapse
item.description: Federal Council report and Ecoplan study: traffic jams for 422,000 hours a day, billion-dollar costs and the collapse of border workers by up to 60% without Schengen.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Council report published on September 18, 2026. - Swiss GDP contraction of up to 3.9% in the event of leaving Schengen. - Annual income loss of up to 1,293 / 1,300 francs per inhabitant. - Collapse of cross-border workers estimated at up to 60%.
## Key facts - Report date: September 18, 2026 - Study conducted by: Ecoplan - Study commissioner: Federal Office of Justice - Expected GDP contraction: Up to 3.9% - Per capita income loss: Up to 1,293 / 1,300 francs per year - Hours lost per day in traffic queues: 422,000 hours - Annual commuting costs: Between 1.08 and 2.27 billion francs
Association with the European Schengen and Dublin agreements guarantees Switzerland enormous economic and internal security advantages, as clearly confirmed by the Federal Council report, adopted on September 18, 2026 on the basis of an analytical study conducted by Ecoplan on behalf of the Federal Office of Justice. The analysis outlines a detailed picture of the socio-economic impacts if Switzerland were to abandon the agreements with the European Union, highlighting price increases, infrastructure paralysis, and severe penalties for border regions such as Canton Ticino. The forecasting data projected to 2035 show scenarios of severe recession in the most unfavorable scenario, including a contraction of Swiss Gross Domestic Product that could suffer a reduction of up to 3.9%. This economic contraction would translate into an income drop of up to 1,293 / 1,300 francs per year per inhabitant. Tourism would also suffer a severe crisis, as the need to apply for a separate Swiss visa would discourage non-EU tourists, with estimated losses for the tourism sector fluctuating between 320 and 810 million francs per year. The lack of fluidity at the border would make the Swiss economic hub less attractive and less competitive on a global scale.
### Economic and tourism scenarios by 2035 Economic projections highlight how the potential abandonment of the European bilateral agreements would create a situation of severe financial instability for the entire Swiss economy. The loss of attractiveness of the economic hub would directly reflect on international markets and Switzerland's ability to attract capital and talent. The tourism sector, in particular, would suffer a very hard blow due to bureaucratic barriers for travelers from third countries, with negative impacts on hotels, restaurants, and related industries. The estimate of losses between 320 and 810 million francs per year captures the vulnerability of a sector heavily dependent on free movement and ease of access to Swiss territory. These dynamics demonstrate how closely the economic stability of the Confederation is tied to the Schengen and Dublin agreements, whose potential termination would trigger a chain reaction capable of hitting every single productive sector, from major financial centers to peripheral and border regions like Canton Ticino, which would bear the brunt of the consequences of a rigid and barely permeable border for goods, services, and people. Without the Schengen Agreement, the border crossings between Switzerland and neighboring countries, including Italy, France, Germany, and Austria, would effectively become external borders of the European Union. This would impose systematic checks on people both entering and exiting, radically altering the daily mobility of workers and citizens. For highly integrated territories such as the Canton of Ticino, Geneva, and Basel, the daily consequences would be immediate and disruptive. The report estimates as many as 422,000 hours lost per day: this is the time commuters would spend stuck in traffic jams at border crossings such as Chiasso, Stabio, or Ponte Tresa on every single working day. In addition to this, travel costs related to delays and traffic would amount to between 1.08 and 2.27 billion Swiss francs per year.
### Impact on mobility and the real estate market The disproportionate increase in waiting times at border crossings could lead to a collapse in cross-border workers, with an estimated reduction of up to 60% in the total number of people crossing the border daily for work. Key sectors such as healthcare, specifically regarding care services, and the restaurant industry would risk total paralysis due to a severe labor shortage. Furthermore, the effects would be heavily felt on the region's real estate market: it is estimated that up to 170,000 people could decide to transfer their residence directly to Switzerland to avoid daily checks and endless queues at the border. This shift in residents would alter demographic balances and housing demand both in Swiss territory and in the Italian border areas, generating tensions on property prices and rents. To understand the magnitude of such transformations, one must consider [border waiting times](nav:border) as a key indicator of cross-border economic fluidity, where every slowdown translates into very high operating costs for companies and a drastic deterioration in the quality of life of commuters who travel daily between Italy and Switzerland for professional reasons.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). Beyond strictly financial and mobility aspects, the Federal Council's report emphasizes the invaluable importance of police cooperation and the management of migratory flows through the European system. In 2025 alone, thanks to the Schengen Information System, Swiss law enforcement recorded approximately 40,000 relevant hits, promptly identifying criminals and dangerous individuals. Without access to this shared database, Switzerland would not be able to guarantee the same security standards, not even by increasing its domestic investments. On the asylum front, exiting the Dublin system would prevent Switzerland from transferring asylum seekers to the first EU entry country. The obligation to examine all applications on its own territory would prolong stay durations, leading to an estimated cost increase between 166 and 824 million francs.
### Why hypothetical savings are not enough The report clarifies a fundamental misunderstanding regarding the alleged financial benefits of a potential exit: any savings resulting from the cessation of contributions paid to the EU for the management of Schengen and Dublin would by no means cover the costs necessary to reintroduce and manage comprehensive border controls, hire new border personnel, upgrade road and customs infrastructure, as well as create and maintain proprietary security databases. item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Withholding tax levied only in Switzerland - Exemptions: 7,500 euros (old) or 10,000 euros (new) - New Agreement in force since January 1, 2024 - Tax credit in Italy to avoid double taxation
## Key facts Frontalieri Agreement: signed 12/23/2020, in force 01/01/2024 Italian Ratification: Law 83 of 06/13/2023 Double Taxation Convention: 12/09/1976 Exemption for New Frontalieri: 10,000 euros Exemption for Old Frontalieri: 7,500 euros IRPEF 23%: up to 28,000 euros
The tax framework for those who work in Switzerland and reside in Italy is governed by precise rules, with particular attention to those who exceed a distance of 20 km. The withholding tax on employment income is levied exclusively in Switzerland. To prevent the worker from paying twice on the same income, Italy applies a tax credit through the CE section of the 730 tax return.
### The new tax regime The New Frontalieri Agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023, entered into force on January 1, 2024. This text defines the basis of current taxation, which will continue through 2026. Since Switzerland is not a member of the EU or EEA, it relies on the Double Taxation Convention signed on December 9, 1976, to coordinate tax flows with the Italian State.
The administration of these taxes is divided between the AFC/ESTV (Federal Tax Administration) at the federal level and the cantonal tax administrations. It is important to clarify that entities such as UFAS or BFS have no power to set tax rates, as they deal respectively with social security and statistics. Workers who acquired frontier worker status before July 17, 2023, benefit from a transitional regime valid until 2033, with an exemption of 7,500 euros, while new entries have an exemption of 10,000 euros. ## Practical Analysis and Tax Scenarios The distinction between cross-border workers residing at different distances from the border, particularly the 20 km limit, influences the perception of the overall tax burden. Although withholding tax is collected in Switzerland, the final calculation in Italy depends on IRPEF rates: 23% for income up to 28,000 euros, 35% between 28,001 and 50,000 euros, and 43% over 50,000 euros.
### Hypothetical Taxation Scenarios To understand the impact, let us consider two scenarios based on the provided exemptions. In a first hypothetical scenario, an 'old' cross-border worker (active before July 17, 2023) applies an exemption of 7,500 euros to their income before calculating the tax impact in Italy. In a second scenario, a 'new' cross-border worker can benefit from the higher exemption of 10,000 euros.
The analysis of the net amount also depends on mandatory Swiss contributions. The payslip shows AVS/AI/IPG deductions at 5.3% borne by the employee, unemployment insurance AD/AC at 1.1% (with a ceiling of 148,200 CHF), and LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5%. To these is added the LPP, which varies between 7% and 18% depending on the age group, starting from age 25.
The comparison between the two regimes shows how the 2024-2033 transitional regime protects long-term workers, while new agreements seek to standardize exemption thresholds. Those residing beyond 20 km must carefully monitor the tax credit to avoid reporting errors that could lead to penalties from the Agenzia delle Entrate. ## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Operational Guide and Steps to Follow To correctly manage taxation in 2026, especially for those residing beyond 20 km, it is necessary to follow a rigorous reporting procedure. Managing the flows between Switzerland and Italy requires precision in the documents submitted to the Agenzia delle Entrate and the MEF.
### Tax Declaration Checklist 1. Retrieval of the Swiss income certificate: a fundamental document issued by the cantonal tax administration. 2. Verification of the applicable exemption: determine whether you fall under the 'old cross-border commuters' (7,500 euro exemption) or the 'new' ones (10,000 euro exemption). 3. Completion of the CE section of the 730 form: entry of taxes paid in Switzerland to request the tax credit and neutralize double taxation. 4. Check of social security contributions: verification of AVS and LPP quotas paid for possible coordination with INPS.
In addition to taxes, the cross-border worker must manage the LAMal health insurance. Holders of a G permit have a right of option for insurance; for adults, the provided deductibles vary from 300 to 2,500 CHF. It is essential that this choice is consistent with one's health situation and budget.

The implementation of the initiative proposed by the SVP would have direct and heavy repercussions on daily mobility. This massive flow, which includes several hundred thousand cross-border commuters, would be overturned by permanent and systematic controls.
### Congestion and traffic costs
The introduction of a complete presence at border crossings would generate what the Government defines as strong pressure on the economy and on commuter traffic. In particular, border areas would suffer a devastating impact due to what would be defined as a congestion cost of billions of francs. This scenario concerns not only the time lost in slowdowns, but the entire economic impact resulting from the inefficiency of border flows.
The Executive also emphasizes that increasing the personnel assigned to border protection would entail high costs, adding a further burden to public coffers. In addition to the direct charges, the risk of compromising well-being in Switzerland is one of the Government's central concerns, which sees this measure as a threat to the country's economic stability.
### The risk to internal security
Contrary to what is claimed by the promoters, the Federal Council believes that systematic controls would not be suitable instruments to curb secondary migration or cross-border crime. The Government reiterates that the current customs system already carries out controls based on the situation and risks, which can be intensified if necessary, without however blocking the entire circulation system.
Another critical point concerns access to data. If Switzerland were to abandon the Schengen/Dublin system to implement the initiative, it would lose access to European research databases. ## In brief - MEF decree signed for funding of border municipalities - Resources allocated to municipalities within 20 km of the border - Territories bordering Ticino, Graubünden, and Valais involved
## Key facts Who: Minister of Economy and Finance Giancarlo Giorgetti What: Decree for the allocation of the state contribution Territorial radius: 20 kilometers from the border line Cantons involved: Ticino, Graubünden, and Valais Funding source: Fund for the economic development of border territories
The Minister of Economy and Finance, Giancarlo Giorgetti, has officially signed the decree defining and allocating the state contribution intended for border municipalities. The act, made known through a direct note from the MEF, represents the definitive turning point for the funding of Italian territories located adjacent to Switzerland. This measure is not an isolated intervention, but the concrete implementation of commitments previously undertaken between the two States.
### The regulatory origin of the intervention The measure is based on agreements signed between Italy and Switzerland within the framework of the historic Rome and Bern Agreement of 2020. The objective is to provide economic resources to those populated centers that, due to their geographical position, manage the complexities related to the constant flow of cross-border workers and residents. The funds necessary for the disbursement are drawn from the Fund for the economic development of border territories, an institution created specifically to mitigate disparities and strengthen marginal areas.
The allocation of resources follows precise geographical criteria. To be considered beneficiaries, Municipalities must be located within a radius of 20 kilometers from the border line. The scope is further defined based on the bordering Swiss territories: the benefit indeed concerns Italian municipalities bordering the Cantons of Ticino, Graubünden, and Valais. This perimeter ensures that the funds reach exactly where the impact of commuting is most pronounced, ensuring that local administrations have the means to manage the infrastructural friction generated by daily flows towards Switzerland. ## Implicazioni per l'area di frontiera L'erogazione di questi fondi ha un impatto diretto sulla qualità della vita di chi attraversa ogni giorno il confine. I lavoratori che possiedono un [permesso G](nav:permits) e risiedono nei comuni beneficiari vedranno un potenziamento dei servizi che utilizzano quotidianamente. Il decreto specifica infatti che le risorse saranno destinate a tre pilastri principali: la crescita economica locale, il potenziamento delle infrastrutture territoriali e il rafforzamento dei servizi pubblici.
### Analisi dei benefici concreti Il potenziamento delle infrastrutture è l'aspetto più critico per il frontaliere. Un incremento dei fondi a disposizione dei Comuni può tradursi in una migliore gestione della viabilità urbana e dei collegamenti verso i valichi. Sebbene il decreto non specifichi singoli progetti, la destinazione d'uso verso le infrastrutture suggerisce un'attenzione verso la mobilità e la manutenzione stradale, elementi essenziali per chi deve raggiungere il posto di lavoro in Canton Ticino nei tempi previsti.
Per quanto riguarda i servizi pubblici, l'attenzione è rivolta specificamente alle comunità di confine e ai lavoratori frontalieri. Questo significa che le amministrazioni comunali potranno investire in servizi di supporto che rendano più efficiente la gestione amministrativa e sociale di una popolazione che vive in un regime di transnazionalità. Il rafforzamento dei servizi pubblici è essenziale per bilanciare il carico che i frontalieri apportano ai servizi locali (come trasporti, gestione rifiuti e manutenzione spazi pubblici) pur versando le imposte alla fonte in Svizzera.
Il sostegno alla crescita economica locale mira a creare un ecosistema più attrattivo anche sul lato italiano. L'idea è che i Comuni di frontiera non siano semplici "dormitori" per chi lavora in Svizzera, ma centri economici vitali. Questo potrebbe portare a un miglioramento dell'offerta commerciale e professionale locale, riducendo la dipendenza esclusiva dal mercato del lavoro elvetico e migliorando la vivibilità complessiva dei centri situati entro i 20 km dal confine.

Municipalities that meet the criteria (within 20 km of the border with Ticino, Grisons, or Valais) will need to coordinate with state authorities for the crediting of contributions.

item.title: Psychic absences in Ticino: 51% end up in dismissal
item.description: In Ticino, 51% of absences due to mental causes lead to the dissolution of the contract. The share of AI beneficiaries for psychiatric reasons rose to 51%.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - 51% of absences due to mental illness in Ticino ends with the termination of the contract - 51% of AI pension recipients in Ticino have psychiatric reasons, compared to 33% twentyyears ago - Absenteeism should be considered a symptom, not the problem itself
- Percentage of mental absences that end in the dissolution of the contract: 51% - Share of AI beneficiaries for psychiatric reasons in Ticino: 51% - Share twentyyears ago: 33% - Priority of Swiss disability insurance: professional reintegration
In 51% of cases, an absence from work related to a mental illness ends with the termination of the contract. And still 51% represents today, in Ticino, the share of beneficiaries of an AI pension for psychiatric reasons, compared to 33% just over twentyyears ago. Two numbers that show how mental discomfort has become one of the central issues in the world of work.
The theme was at the center of a conference organized in Mendrisio da Compasso, where it emerged that mental health is less and less a taboo, but where the early recognition of signs of difficulty remains crucial.
"You lose contacts, you lose the habit of working," Marzio Proietti, vice president of Compasso, explains to the RSI Newspaper. For this reason, he stresses, it is important to encourage a gradual return, without putting pressure on the employee and also providing for trial periods.
### The Role of Disability Insurance
The logic of ## Practical analysis: what changes for workers and companies
The two key figures — 51% of contract terminations due to mental health absences and 51% of disability insurance beneficiaries for psychiatric reasons — are no coincidence. They represent a significant increase compared to the 33% recorded twenty years ago, indicating that mental distress is becoming a central issue in the Swiss labor market.
### The human and business cost
The cost is not only for those who suffer: we companies risk losing collaborators, experience, and skills. And when an absence is prolonged, the chances of an effective reintegration decrease. This is particularly relevant for cross-border workers, who commute daily between Italy and Switzerland, where every day of absence can compromise the work routine.
For workers with G or B permits, prolonged absenteeism can have direct consequences on access to the LAMal health insurance and disability insurance coverage. Early recognition of signals therefore becomes a systemic issue, not just an individual one.
### Risk factors and burnout
The factors that can foster stress conditions up to burnout are varied: lack of recognition and appreciation, a difficult relationship with superiors or colleagues, a non-serene work environment, and the absence of a clear separation between professional and private life. According to Renato Dotti, president of the Forum Gestione Salute in Azienda, leadership is needed that is first and foremost capable of listening to the needs of collaborators.
This means building a 'positive environment' and creating that psychological safety that allows people to express their discomfort, but also to talk about mistakes without feeling immediately exposed or judged. For cross-border workers, often subject to double stress (work and cross-border family life), this safety is fundamental.
### The before and after comparison
Twenty years ago, 33% of disability pension beneficiaries had psychiatric reasons. Today that 33% has become 51%. This shift indicates that the Swiss healthcare and social security system is experiencing an exponential growth in cases related to mental health. For companies, intervening before a situation of vulnerability turns into a long absence means not only saving skills but also reducing absenteeism costs.
A structured approach — with gradual returns, probation periods, and active listening — can produce benefits for both parties: 'The employer does not lose the skills of their collaborator and the worker does not lose their job'.

item.title: Seizure of protected parrots at the Gandria crossing
item.description: A Swiss citizen was stopped at the Gandria crossing with two ash parrots without Cites authorization. Intervention by UDSC and USAV.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Swiss citizen stopped at the Gandria border crossing - Transporting two African grey parrots in the car - The animals belong to a protected species - Cites import authorization was missing
## Key facts - Date: Thursday, September 10 - Location: Gandria border crossing - Authorities: FOCBS and FSVO officers - Species: African grey parrots (Appendix I) - Vehicle: Car with Swiss license plates
Officers of the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) recently intercepted and seized two birds during a routine check at a border crossing. The incident took place on Thursday, September 10, when a Swiss citizen was stopped at the Gandria border crossing while traveling in a car with Swiss license plates. Inside the vehicle, customs officers discovered the presence of two African grey parrots. The driver was in no way in possession of the authorization required by law to import protected specimens. The timely intervention of the border authorities made it possible to block the illegal transport of these particular exotic animals, which fall fully into categories protected at the international level.
### The intervention of customs and veterinary authorities Immediately after the initial check carried out by FOCBS officers, the birds were immediately impounded. The operation took place on the specific order of the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO). Given the total absence of the documentation required for customs clearance, the two animals were seized with an absolute ban on the owner being able to dispose of them in any way. The competent authorities continue to monitor compliance with customs regulations regarding the transit of protected wildlife species, reminding everyone that every cross-border movement of animals covered by protection agreements must be accompanied by the relevant official permits issued by the designated bodies before travel. ### The owner's statements and the origins of the birds During the checks carried out at the Gandria border crossing, the owner of the two African grey parrots provided his version of the facts to the intervening customs officers. The man stated that he had purchased the birds directly from a private breeder. According to what was reported by the Swiss motorist himself, the seller did not provide him with any Cites certificate at the time of the transfer of the animals. This lack of primary documentation immediately triggered in-depth checks by the FOCBS, as current legislation does not allow exceptions based on the buyer's good faith or the failure to deliver documents by the private seller.
### The species' protection level The owner's situation worsened further due to the particular zoological classification of the transported birds. The African grey parrots in question actually belong to a species listed in Appendix I of protection of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (Cites). This is the highest level of protection provided by the international convention, reserved exclusively for species that are concretely at risk of extinction and whose international trade or transit is strictly regulated and restricted to exceptional and rigorously authorized cases. The total absence of the Cites attestation associated with such a high level of protection explains the firmness with which the FOCBS and the FSVO proceeded with the immediate seizure of the parrots at the border crossing.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Procedures for the transit of protected animals Anyone who needs to transport animals or specimens of protected species across borders must comply with a series of very specific formal procedures established by international conventions and adopted by the federal authorities. Before planning any movement involving customs clearance, it is essential to check the status of the species by consulting the official Cites lists. For animals falling under Annex I, such as the African grey parrots involved in the check at Gandria, it is mandatory to obtain in advance the import and export permits issued by the competent offices. Purchasing from private breeders in no way exempts the buyer from the burden of demanding and verifying the presence of all original documentation before traveling in their own vehicle.
### Tools for customs verification and in-depth analysis To avoid administrative or criminal penalties and the consequent seizure of the animals, it is necessary to regularly consult the directives published by the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (OSAV) and the FOCBS regarding tourist and commercial traffic of goods and protected species. Travelers and commuters who regularly cross customs checkpoints must pay the utmost attention to regulations on the protection of fauna and flora. To learn more about the rules and tariffs applied to the transit of goods and commodities, you can consult our official [calculator](nav:calculator) dedicated to tax and customs checks.

item.title: Pension Switzerland: Record 725-point Raiffeisen Barometer
item.description: The Raiffeisen and ZHAW barometer reaches the record of 725 points. Pillar 3a grows to 79%, but uncertainty remains over the financing of the AVS.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Raiffeisen and ZHAW barometer at 725 points - First pillar financing and Old Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) among concerns - 39% fear that OASI will not cover expenses - Pillar 3a reaches a new high of 79%
## Key facts - Organization: Raiffeisen and ZHAW - Barometer value: 725 points out of 1000 - Increase: plus 28 points compared to the previous year - Initial value 2018: 587 points - Survey sample: over 1000 people aged between 18 and 65 - OASI concern: 39% of respondents - Pillar 3a share: 79% of the population - Awareness of the new Pillar 3a rule: 63% of the sample - Supplementary contribution: 5% of the sample
The situation of the Swiss pension system is showing further improvement, according to the latest Raiffeisen barometer, produced in collaboration with ZHAW, the Zurich University of Applied Sciences. Driving this progress are primarily the better financial situation of pension funds and a higher savings rate among the population, elements that have directly impacted overall economic conditions. The Risk and Insurance Institute of ZHAW highlighted how economic factors have generated a favorable context. Compared to the previous year, the barometer value rose by twenty-eight points, reaching seven hundred and twenty-five points out of a maximum of one thousand. In the first survey in 2018, the recorded points were five hundred and eighty-seven. This is the highest level since the beginning of the research conducted by the sponsoring entities, signaling a positive dynamic for the Swiss pension system. The overall improvement is primarily due to the good financial conditions of all three pension pillars, but the survey also combines economic indicators with data from a survey conducted on over one thousand people aged between eighteen and sixty-five. This sample provides a picture that highlights not only positive aspects but also persistent elements of uncertainty regarding the future sustainability of the system. The major concern detected among the population remains the long-term financing of the first pillar, with 39% of respondents fearing that OASI will no longer be able to cover its expenses in the future. This data reflects a widespread climate of apprehension among workers regarding the stability of basic public pension benefits in the coming years. In-depth data analysis shows how private pension savings continue to play a central role for resident citizens and for those planning their professional and financial future in Swiss territory, dealing with current rules and regulatory developments concerning occupational pensions and individual provident pillars. Those who wish to delve deeper into retirement planning and understand how contributions work can regularly consult the tools dedicated to [pension planning](nav:pension) to navigate the different pillars of the Swiss system. Alongside fears regarding the financial sustainability of the first pillar and the relevant public institution, data collected by the survey show a growing trend toward voluntary individual pension savings. Increasingly more people are setting aside sums in anticipation of old age, and the share of respondents who own or contribute to a pillar 3a has reached a new high of seventy-nine percent. Further impetus to this form of private savings may have come from the possibility, introduced at the beginning of twenty-twenty-six, to retroactively fill contribution gaps in the third pillar segment. The potential in this regard nevertheless remains broad within the active population. Sixty-three percent are aware of the new rule introduced, but only five percent have actually made a supplementary payment to cover uncovered periods. This discrepancy between the theoretical knowledge of the rule and its concrete application highlights how individual financial planning requires resources and accurate assessments by individual taxpayers. Another aspiration frequently mentioned but particularly difficult to achieve for many workers is early retirement, which often remains a wish rather than a concrete reality. More than half of people aged between fifty-one and sixty-five would like to leave the workforce before the ordinary retirement age, but at the same time almost a third believe they cannot realize this dream due to economic conditions and the requirements necessary to sustain the annuity over time. Financing early retirement will be even more challenging for future generations due to falling conversion rates, higher life expectancy, and increasingly non-linear working careers, as warned by the research institute's experts. Consequently, a potential longer stay in the Swiss professional world also gains greater importance. For about two-thirds of the interviewed sample, working longer would in principle be conceivable, but for most people this option is only viable on a targeted basis or part-time, balancing income needs with the sustainability of work commitment at an advanced age.

The complexity of the social security system requires a careful analysis of the options available to those who work or intend to work in Switzerland, taking into account the deadlines and rules governing mandatory and optional contributions. The dynamics highlighted by the Raiffeisen barometer offer concrete insights for those who must manage their social security position between the first, second and third pillars, carefully evaluating the savings prospects and supplementary payment options introduced by recent legislation. To effectively plan your provisions and check the impact of contributions on your future pension, it is advisable to use the calculation and simulation tools available online.
