Railway stations in Ticino represent much more than just a transit place for the thousands of commuters who use the connections every day to travel across the region. For tourists and visitors, they constitute the first direct contact with the cities and the canton, effectively acting as a true calling card. For this very reason, it is essential that railway stations—considering both the main hubs located in urban centers and the regional and secondary ones scattered across various areas—manage to guarantee adequate and constant standards of order, cleanliness, decorum, and safety. This is the extreme summary of the official parliamentary question submitted by Daniele Piccaluga, member and coordinator of the Lega dei Ticinesi, to the attention of the Ticino Council of State.

Over the past few months, according to what was highlighted by the Grand Council member, various news reports and numerous testimonies publicly shared by citizens on social media platforms have strongly drawn attention to widespread situations of hardship detected inside railway stations and in the immediately surrounding areas. Among the reported issues are acts of vandalism, presence of filth, damage to structures, individuals harassing travelers in transit, episodes of theft, and various behaviors capable of generating a general sense of insecurity, a perception that tends to intensify particularly during evening hours. The safety of users must not be evaluated solely through objective parameters linked to law enforcement interventions, but requires similar attention toward the perceived safety of those who use public transport on a daily basis.

### The perception of safety among travelers

Students, commuting workers, the elderly, families, and all those people who, especially in the evening, find themselves having to wait alone for a train connection or a bus transfer often express concern in the face of such contexts of degradation. The Ticino deputy specifically recalled the recent cases that occurred at the railway stations of Bellinzona and Mendrisio, episodes that ended up at the center of cantonal media attention, amply demonstrating how the problem deserves careful institutional consideration. Similarly, comparable situations of hardship, acts of vandalism, or critical issues related to safety have been reported over time in other realities present across the cantonal territory, highlighting a trend that is not limited to a single railway station but potentially affects the entire local public transport network. The Swiss Federal Railways themselves, as recalled in the text of the parliamentary question submitted by the representative of the Lega dei Ticinesi, clearly state within their own regulations the primary objective of ensuring stations that are always safe, fully functional, and clean for users. The company's provisions already include precise rules aimed at countering nuisance behavior, acts of vandalism, the uncontrolled dumping of waste, and any other form of degradation that could compromise the usability of collective spaces. The intent of the parliamentary act is certainly not to criminalize certain categories of people, but rather to reaffirm a fundamental and straightforward principle: public spaces intended for collective transport must be able to be used peacefully by all citizens and constantly maintained in decent conditions.
Over recent years, public institutions at various levels have exerted considerable financial and organizational efforts. The Canton, the Confederation, the Municipalities, and transport companies have invested substantial financial resources with the stated objective of enhancing and making regional and national public transport collectively more attractive. In this scenario, it would be profoundly contradictory to decide to increase the frequencies of connections, implement new runs, and proceed with the modernization of material infrastructures without paying the same attention and care to the quality, cleanliness, and security of the physical spaces through which users daily access the mobility network.
### Monitoring of secondary stations
The problem highlighted by the Grand Councillor does not exclusively concern large urban railway stations located in the main centers such as Bellinzona, Lugano, Locarno, Mendrisio, and Chiasso. In secondary and regional stations, especially with the arrival of evening and night hours, the lesser physical presence of railway personnel or on-site surveillance makes the importance of ensuring regular and constant monitoring of the overall conditions of spaces, cleanliness, public lighting, and perceived security levels even more crucial.

Starting from these premises and detailed considerations, the parliamentary question submits a series of specific questions to the Ticino Government to clarify the true extent of the phenomenon. First, it asks whether the Council of State currently possesses a comprehensive and updated assessment of the situation regarding decorum, cleanliness, and security of all Ticino railway stations, including secondary and peripheral locations. It also inquires what official reports regarding security issues, acts of vandalism, damage, or marked degradation have been received over the last three years by the Cantonal Police or other competent services of the cantonal administration.
A further central aspect concerns the existence or absence of structured and coordinated monitoring among the various institutional and operational actors—namely the Canton, Municipalities, SBB, TILO, Transport Police, and the various cantonal and municipal police forces—aimed at promptly identifying the stations or time slots presenting the greatest critical issues. It is then asked whether the Government currently considers the standards of cleanliness, routine and extraordinary maintenance, night lighting, and surveillance of Ticino stations satisfactory, with a particular emphasis on regional and secondary stations. Finally, clarifications are requested on the procedures by which situations of degradation found by local authorities are reported to SBB and what the average technical intervention times are.

The final questions posed to the Council of State concern the executive's willingness to formally request SBB to adopt a specific and targeted intervention plan for the Ticino territory, aimed at ensuring adequate, uniform, and homogeneous standards of order, cleanliness, and maintenance in both main and secondary hubs. item.description: The General Assembly of the CGIL meeting in Rome elected Stefania Filetti by secret ballot in the new confederal secretariat composed of ten people.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Stefania Filetti elected to the national secretariat of Cgil - A journey that began in the Alfa Romeo factory - Secret ballot by the general assembly gathered in Rome - Ten members in the new confederal secretariat
What: Election to the national secretariat of Cgil Who: Stefania Filetti Where: Rome Organization: Cgil Previous role: General Secretary of Cgil Varese
The general assembly of Cgil, meeting in Rome, elected Stefania Filetti by secret ballot to the organization's new confederal secretariat. The nomination proposal came directly from General Secretary Maurizio Landini, placing Filetti within a renewed team of ten people, evenly divided between five women and five men. This election represents the highest point of a long trade union career that has its roots in Italian industrial departments and has developed through a rigorous path, step by step, without sudden leaps or external accelerations compared to daily groundwork in workplaces.
### From the blue collar to the national secretariat Stefania Filetti's trade union history began in the late 1980s at the Alfa Romeo plant in Arese, a large factory she entered with a work-training contract. This was one of the last generations of workers hired after the factory's transfer to Fiat. Assigned to the mechanics department, Filetti began experiencing the reality of industrial production and the factory every day. It was precisely within that department, in the early 1990s, that she took the first step in her representation activity, becoming a Fiom delegate. This was not an arrival from the outside or from bureaucratic structures, but an experience born directly from the production line and daily contact with the working conditions of her colleagues. Her commitment was consolidated in 1992 with her first official steps as a trade union delegate, laying the groundwork for a gradual transition to roles of greater responsibility within the structure of Fiom Milan, in the historic Sempione area, which took place in 1998 when she became a trade union official. ### Territorial roots in the Varese area Stefania Filetti's journey continues and takes deep roots in the provincial territory starting from 2005, the year she joined the Fiom of Varese. This stage marks a further deepening of the dynamics related to metalworking and local industrial disputes. Two years after her arrival in the Varese structure, she was elected to the metalworkers' secretariat, and then in 2011 she took on the role of general secretary of the category. Here too, her growth took place entirely within the blue-collar category from which her professional and trade union experience had started. Subsequently, her scope of action expanded from the category dimension to the general confederal dimension of the Cgil of Varese. In 2013 she joined the provincial secretariat and in 2018 she assumed the position of organizational secretary, a managerial and political role that allowed her to get to know in detail the complex territorial organization of the organization, including the Chambers of Labour, the trade union offices and the Spi locations.
June 2020 marks another fundamental step with her election as general secretary of the Cgil of Varese, succeeding Umberto Colombo. During the years spent at the head of the Varese Chamber of Labour, Filetti managed a particularly complex period characterized by industrial crises, open trade union disputes, the constant defense of employment and wages, as well as issues related to precariousness and safety in the workplace. In recent years, she has directly addressed the mobilizations promoted by Cgil on referendums concerning work and citizenship, the defense of public healthcare and the protection of workers in contracting out. The approach given to her work finds synthesis in a reflection expressed precisely in 2020: when an idea and a thought become a collective condition shared by the majority, the growth of the common line transforms into authentic trade union militancy. An approach that ideally unites her origins in the factory with the top confederal responsibilities assumed today at the national level.

The uniqueness of this career lies in the absence of shortcuts or level jumps: every role was preceded by hands-on experience in the field, moving from factory worker to union delegate, from official to secretariat member, until holding the position of general secretary of the provincial Fiom first and of the Varese Cgil later. item.title: FFS cargo cuts: Bern responds to Ticino
item.description: The federal government rejects the resolution of the Canton of Ticino on the cuts of FFS Cargo, confirming the management autonomy of the company and the centrality of the north-south axis.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bern does not intervene on SBB Cargo cuts - The canton's parliamentary resolution rejected - No room for strategic change - Centrality of the north-south corridor confirmed
## Key facts - Questioned: Albert Rösti - Recipient: Daria Lepori - Period of cuts: 2025 and this year - Destination of the letter: President of the Grand Council
The freight traffic landscape along the north-south axis records a clear stance by the federal government regarding the parliamentary resolution submitted to counter the dismantling of SBB Cargo's activities in the Canton of Ticino. Arriving during the summer on the desk of Grand Council President Daria Lepori, the official response signed by the head of the Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications, Albert Rösti, formally closes the door to any corrective intervention by Bern. The federal executive reiterates its firm intention to strictly apply the legal provisions currently in force, maintaining a line of consistency with respect to the framework conditions established at the national level for the transport market. The stance comes following the resolution submitted to the Federal Palace in the month of May, a political act born with the objective of mobilizing central institutions in the face of operational reductions implemented by the Swiss Federal Railways between 2025 and the current year, which first hit the combined transport sector and subsequently that of single wagonload freight. On decisions of an occupational and internal nature to the company, the Federal Council's note is unequivocal, specifying that such choices fall entirely within the management autonomy of SBB, without the government exercising direct influence. The political direction of the Federal Executive toward the transport company materializes solely through the definition of strategic objectives assigned to the owner, while operational management remains entrusted to market dynamics within the general regulatory framework. Despite concerns raised at the cantonal level for the economic and logistical future of the region, the Federal Council expressed satisfaction that no outright layoffs occurred in Ticino, highlighting that the affected staff were able to benefit from internal relocation options, with over half of the workers involved continuing to operate in the rail freight traffic sector.
### The centrality of the transalpine railway line
In the official document transmitted to the Ticino authorities, the central government strongly reiterates that the strategic centrality of the Canton of Ticino along the north-south transit axis remains a fixed point of federal transport policy. However, this territorial confirmation does not translate into a brake on corporate decisions adopted by the railway management. According to what was clarified by the head of the competent federal department, there are no regulatory or political prerequisites for the transport company to back down on the decisions undertaken, nor are there margins for action for the federal government to impose a change in the strategic course undertaken by the railway company. The planning and execution of the operational cuts reflect the structural setup defined by current regulations, leaving unchanged the perimeter of action within which SBB manages its commercial traffic flows and heavy rail transport logistics. The in-depth analysis of the response received from Bern highlights complex dynamics that characterize the relationship between the business choices of large public service companies and the institutional expectations of peripheral or border regions. The stance expressed by the Federal Council highlights a gap between the requests for intervention formulated by local political bodies and the constitutional and legal limits that regulate the action of the central administration regarding former federal monopolies. For economic operators and for those who live and work in the cross-border fabric, these business decisions reflect a profound transformation of the logistics and transport sector, where competitive pressure and the pursuit of economic efficiency end up prevailing over traditional functions of capillary service to the territory. The decision to abandon a binding modal shift objective for domestic freight traffic, decided by parliament during the recent total revision of the freight transport law, demonstrates that the reference legislative framework does not provide specific coercive instruments to force the movement of goods by rail outside of the major trans-Alpine routes. This legislative approach consolidates a market regime in which SBB's business choices enjoy a wide margin of maneuver, aimed at restoring financial health and optimizing operational processes, even when this entails a contraction of regional services linked to single-wagonload freight or proximity combined transport.
### Future scenarios for freight transport and regional logistics
The repercussions of this political and economic orientation extend well beyond the immediate trade union or employment dispute, directly touching the overall logistical architecture of the Ticino territory. The confirmation that current instruments for the promotion of rail freight traffic are considered adequate by the federal government excludes the introduction of new mandates or targeted subsidies to support unprofitable domestic traffic. For Ticino companies that depend on rail freight transport, the panorama outlined by Bern's response imposes a strategic reflection on the supply chain and the need to integrate with the main logistical corridors, accepting a model in which proximity services undergo progressive dismantling in favor of centralized hubs. The transition of personnel, while having avoided mass layoffs thanks to internal relocation measures, still marks a contraction of direct operational presence in the cantonal territory, reducing the capillarity of railway logistics skills available locally. The current situation confirms that the Swiss freight transport market is moving towards greater corporate concentration, leaving cantonal authorities with limited room for maneuver to influence the industrial strategies of a federal company that responds primarily to budget and efficiency constraints established by the owner and by federal public transport laws.

item.title: Because developing new drugs costs more and more
item.description: In 2024, the average cost to develop a new drug reached $2.23 billion, an increase of 65% compared to 2014.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Average drug development cost at $2.23 billion in 2024 - 65% increase compared to 2014, about 25% with inflation - Trump calls for Europe to pay more for new medicines - Zero duties on generics then massive increases according to the administration
## Key facts Development cost 2024: $2.23 billion Increase compared to 2014: 65% in raw percentage Historical comparison: 30% more than in 2012 according to Tufts Oncology weight: 41% of all clinical trials Incidence of rare cancers: 74% of oncology studies started in 2024 Biopharmaceutical companies: 20 largest in the world analyzed by Deloitte
President Donald Trump has repeated it several times: according to him, European governments benefit from US pharmaceutical spending without contributing enough. Higher prices paid in the United States, he says, generate the profits that fund research and innovation from which the rest of the world also benefits. That's why Europe should pay more for new medicines, Trump says. The tenant of the White House reports that customs tariffs remain on standby until 2028, but then they will be 100% for a year and 200% thereafter, as highlighted in a previous in-depth analysis. How true is this statement? The point is difficult to verify, also because the relationship between development costs and drug prices remains one of the most opaque aspects of the pharmaceutical industry. Developing a drug has always been difficult and characterized by a high percentage of clinical failures, but today the nature of the medicines on which global scientific research focuses has also changed. Many new treatments are biologically more complex, and this exponentially increases the costs of research, laboratory work, and industrial production. For decades, many of the best-selling drugs were small chemical molecules, usually taken in the form of pills: statins to lower cholesterol, antidepressants, painkillers like aspirin. Today, companies are moving toward more complex research areas: specialized drugs, gene therapies, and highly specialized treatments for smaller groups of patients, explains Amanda Cole, director at the Office of Health Economics. This category includes, for example, RNA-based therapies, such as mRNA vaccines against Covid-19, cell and gene therapies, and monoclonal antibodies. The latter are proteins produced in the laboratory: they work similarly to natural antibodies and are designed to recognize specific targets. Keytruda, an immunotherapy used in the treatment of certain cancers, is one such key example. These are drugs that can offer great value to patients, but developing them is an extraordinary scientific and economic challenge. For a long time, pharmaceutical innovation focused on parts of the body that scientists knew relatively well, whereas today entirely unprecedented biological frontiers are being explored that require cutting-edge diagnostic tools and technologies. This transition pushes the overall average cost for each single approved drug upward, highlighting how the data in the Deloitte report reflect a structural transformation of the entire international pharmaceutical sector and its related corporate business models.

The increasing complexity of research is also directly reflected in the type of clinical studies needed to obtain regulatory approvals from competent authorities worldwide. According to IQVIA, oncology now accounts for 41% of all clinical trials, and 74% of oncology trials initiated in 2024 evaluated drugs for rare cancers. Finding eligible patients for such targeted trials requires much longer timeframes, global hospital networks, and highly specialized centers. At the same time, the economic and regulatory landscape continues to evolve under the pressure of international political statements and trade policies that could redefine the cash flows of major pharmaceutical multinationals. ## In brief - 51% of absences due to psychological reasons lead to contract termination - 51% of disability insurance (AI) beneficiaries in Ticino suffer from psychiatric disorders - Early intervention increases the chances of retaining one's job - Mental health has become a central issue in the labor market
## Key facts - Percentage of absences leading to contract termination: 51% - Percentage of disability insurance (AI) beneficiaries due to psychiatric reasons: 51% - Percentage of disability insurance (AI) beneficiaries twenty years ago: 33% - Cited source: Compasso
In the context of the Canton Ticino labor market, managing absences related to psychiatric conditions represents a growing challenge for companies and workers, including the numerous cross-border commuters operating in the territory. According to the data, 51% of work absences caused by psychiatric illnesses end in the definitive termination of the employment contract. This figure, analyzed in conjunction with the share of disability insurance (AI) beneficiaries for psychiatric reasons, which is also at 51% in Ticino compared to the 33% recorded just over twenty years ago, outlines a scenario where mental distress heavily impacts professional stability. The issue was placed at the center of a conference organized by Compasso, an organization that deals with professional reintegration, highlighting how absenteeism should be considered a symptom of a pre-existing fragility rather than the main problem. The loss of collaborators, in addition to representing a human cost, translates into a dispersion of skills and experience for Ticino companies.
### The centrality of timely intervention The ability to recognize signs of difficulty before the situation degenerates is crucial to avoid definitive exit from the labor market. As explained by Marzio Proietti, vice president of Compasso, the main risk linked to prolonged absence is that the worker loses contact with the professional environment and the habit of working. The primary objective, also shared by the disability insurance office, is professional reintegration. Monica Maestri Crivelli, head of the Disability Insurance Office, reiterates that the priority is to identify at-risk situations to allow the person to maintain their resources. Timely action by employers not only reduces costs related to absenteeism but protects the human capital within the company, preventing a phase of fragility from turning into a condition of permanent disability. The suggested approach aims at a gradual reintegration that protects both the company, which does not lose the collaborator, and the worker, who maintains their position and income. The analysis of the factors contributing to burnout reveals a complexity that goes beyond simple absence management. In companies operating in the Canton of Ticino, the onset of professional stress conditions is often correlated with structural elements of the work environment. Renato Dotti, president of the Forum Gestione Salute in Azienda, emphasizes how a lack of recognition, difficult relationships with management or colleagues, and the inability to separate private life from work are catalysts for deep distress. The challenge for corporate leadership is not just to manage absences, but to build an environment characterized by psychological safety. This implies the possibility for the worker to express their discomfort or discuss their mistakes without fear of judgment or negative repercussions. Such a preventive approach, based on active listening to employee needs, is essential to prevent the deterioration of mental health.
### Differences between prevention and absence management Overcoming the taboo surrounding mental health is a first step, but translating this awareness into concrete corporate practices remains the real litmus test. For a worker, including the vast number of cross-border commuters who travel daily through border crossings like Brogeda, the awareness that an absence is a warning signal is fundamental. When a prolonged absence occurs, the success rate of reintegration tends to drop drastically over time. Therefore, the management strategy must focus on a gradual return. This path can include trial periods or adapted tasks, which allow the worker to regain confidence and operational capacity without being subjected to excessive pressure. This is an investment that companies must evaluate carefully, considering the cost of losing specialized skills versus the cost of a well-structured reintegration plan. For those working in Ticino, understanding the dynamics of this support is an essential element for protecting one's career. Firstly, it is essential that the employee does not isolate the problem, communicating with their supervisor or human resources as soon as the first signs of discomfort or difficulty manifest. Timeliness allows for the activation of support measures before the absence becomes prolonged and, consequently, more difficult to manage. For their part, companies should establish protocols that provide for listening and support, integrating, where necessary, collaboration with disability insurance offices to define targeted professional reintegration paths. The priority, as reiterated by institutions, remains keeping the worker within the productive circuit through the recovery of their resources.

It is important to agree with the employer on a return plan that does not put the individual under pressure, possibly providing for a reduced workload initially or flexibility in hours, should the situation require it. ## In brief - EU proposal for a digital social security passport - Digitalization of diplomas and educational qualifications - Rules that also concern Switzerland
## Key facts - Proposing body: European Commission - Initiative name: European Social Security Pass - Presented to: European Parliament in Strasbourg - Presented by: Roxana Minzatu
The European Commission has put forward a proposal to introduce a continental digital social security passport, known as the European Social Security Pass or Esspass. The initiative, presented to the European Parliament in Strasbourg by European Commission Vice-President Roxana Minzatu, aims to simplify administrative procedures related to cross-border activities for entrepreneurs and facilitate the verification of documents by competent labor inspectorates. In detail, the legislative package provides for the revision of two regulations and also affects Switzerland. When a European Union company carries out work activities in the Confederation, in fact, it is required to take charge of the insurance for posted workers. Currently, the relative certification is issued in paper format, but the adjustment presented in Strasbourg provides that in the future it can also be issued in digital format.
### The European regulatory framework and Swiss involvement Switzerland should adopt the regulatory amendments introduced by the European Union, as they are part of the agreement on the free movement of persons. This was confirmed by an EU official contacted by the Keystone-ATS press agency. The measure is part of a broader package prepared by the European Commission and aimed at ensuring fair labor mobility. In addition to the digital passport, the package includes specific provisions on qualification certificates and the strengthening of the European Labour Authority, the agency established to ensure that rules on the coordination of social security are applied in a simple, effective, and fair manner in all EU Member States. ### The digitalization of diplomas and professional titles Among the new developments presented in Strasbourg is a targeted measure for the digitalization of school and professional documents. Based on the European Commission's proposal, diplomas and educational qualifications must be issued in digital format following uniform standards. This technical evolution aims to simplify and accelerate the document verification procedures by the authorities of another country. Despite the digitalization of formats and the harmonization of standards, the decision regarding the formal recognition of qualifications will still remain the exclusive competence of the national authorities of individual countries. This specific proposal is of direct interest and concrete relevance also for Switzerland, which will have to deal with the new digital standards for educational qualifications in the context of cross-border relations and the movement of professionals.
### The scope of interventions and the institutions involved While the provisions concerning social security and the digitalization of educational qualifications directly affect the Swiss Confederation through the agreement on the free movement of persons, other aspects of the European regulatory package follow different paths. In particular, the strengthening of the European Labour Authority does not concern the Confederation. The aforementioned authority has the specific purpose of supporting the national authorities of member countries and acting as a mediator when disputes arise between the various member states of the European Union. Regarding the institutional process of the presented innovations, the proposals formulated by the EU executive will now have to pass the examination of the European Union legislators, namely the European Parliament and the European Council, before proceeding towards effective adoption and the subsequent phase of transposition by interested third countries, including Switzerland.

The proposals presented by the European Commission in Strasbourg have been forwarded to the EU legislators, namely the European Parliament and the European Council, bodies tasked with examining the text, discussing any amendments, and proceeding with the final approval process. Once the legislative path within the European institutions is completed, the adaptation phase will begin for the countries involved. As for Switzerland, the transposition of the amendments concerning the digital social security passport and the digitalization of diplomas will take place within the framework of the bilateral agreement on the free movement of persons, as specified by EU officials contacted by the Keystone-SDA agency. item.title: Ticino Plummeting Rentals: 10.9% Decline in Listings
item.description: For the first time, listings in Switzerland are down. In Ticino the decline reaches 10.9% with an average of 1'501 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Decrease in advertised rents in Switzerland by 1.7% - Drop of 10.9% recorded in Ticino - Vacancy rate at 1.92%
- Report date: Sep 15, 2026 - Institute: Swiss Real Estate Institute - Average rent in Ticino: 1,501 francs - Most expensive municipality: Collina d’Oro 2,400 francs - Most affordable municipality: Bodio 990 francs
For the first time since the 2019/20 period, advertised rents in Switzerland recorded an average decrease of 1.7% between July 2025 and the same month in 2026. This analysis emerges from the latest Rental Home Market Price Analysis by the Swiss Real Estate Institute produced for newhome, based on data published on major Swiss real estate portals. The real estate market is going through a phase of profound evolution, where the dynamics between supply and demand are reflected differently depending on the various regions and housing types present across the federal territory.
### The national and regional overview
The most marked decline at the national level is observed in the Canton of Ticino, where advertised rental prices dropped by 10.9%, settling at an average value of 1,501 francs per month. This is followed by the Canton of Zurich with a 3.3% decrease and the Espace Mittelland with a 0.9% reduction. In contrast to these areas, Central Switzerland recorded a rent increase of 2.3%, while Eastern Switzerland marked a 1.4% increase. Zurich firmly confirms itself as the most expensive region in the entire Confederation, with an average monthly net rent of 2,340 francs, while the Espace Mittelland remains the most economical area at 1,452 francs per month for tenants.
Analyzing the Swiss data in detail, the situation highlights marked heterogeneity among the various cantons and different geographical areas. The Lake Lugano area, while remaining the most expensive in Ticino, shows significantly lower values compared to previous periods. Roman Timm, CEO of newhome.ch AG, highlights how today local situations relating to supply and demand are clearly more relevant and heterogeneous compared to national average values, requiring greater attention to individual regional specificities for anyone wishing to understand the dynamics of the current real estate sector. The Ticino real estate market stands out clearly in the Swiss panorama not only for the sharp contraction in advertised prices, but also for the particularity of the data relating to existing properties. The rent for existing properties in Ticino stands at 1,245 francs, making it the lowest among all six regions analyzed nationwide and positioning itself at a level 16% lower than the overall Swiss average. At the same time, the rent for properties on offer exceeds that of existing properties by 17%, highlighting a significant gap between existing lease agreements and new proposals published on real estate portals.
### Variations in municipalities and housing types
The most expensive Ticinese municipalities historically remain those located around Lake Lugano, although current prices are noticeably lower than in the past. Collina d'Oro leads the cantonal ranking with an average value of 2,400 francs, followed by Morcote with 2,300 francs and Paradiso with 1,900 francs. At the opposite end of the ranking, among the most economical municipalities in the Ticino region, Bodio is noted with 990 francs, Balerna with 1,020 francs, and Chiasso with 1,040 francs per month.
The increase in real estate supply has generated a drop in prices in almost all types of municipalities present in Ticino. In peri-urban municipalities, prices recorded a decrease of 13.3%, against an increase in supply of 15.7%. In rural municipalities, the price drop stands at 8.6%, accompanied by a 25.8% increase in listings. The only exception is represented by high-income municipalities, where prices have remained stable thanks to a contraction in supply equal to 13.9%. Regarding housing types, the most consistent drops affect studio apartments at 11.1% and apartments with 5 or more rooms at 10.6%. Three-room apartments, which represent the most widespread type on the market, show a decrease of 7.5% against a 15.7% growth in supply in this specific category. Studio apartments, characterized by a median rent of 800 francs, constitute the most economically accessible housing solution.

Despite the price decreases recorded in recent months, the Canton of Ticino continues to show the highest vacancy rate for apartments in all of Switzerland, standing at 1.92%, a percentage that is almost double the national average of 1.00%. However, the current figure is down compared to the peak reached during 2021, representing a clear sign that the progressive expansion of supply is slowly but steadily absorbing the demand in the Ticino region.
### Investment dynamics and market prospects
The emerging data refutes certain beliefs widespread among economic operators regarding investor strategies. Professor Peter Ilg, director of the Swiss Real Estate Institute, explains how the trend recorded in the Zurich region categorically refutes the idea that owners and investors prefer to keep apartments vacant rather than reduce rents. Over the last three periods examined, an increasing number of real estate listings have been published and, at the same time, rents have decreased. If investors had hoarded apartments, leaving them deliberately vacant, the volume of empty units would have grown even further.

## In brief - MeMe Project for acoustic rehabilitation of A2 between Mendrisio and Melano - Design publication until 13 October in the municipalities of Val Mara and Mendrisio - Interventions on asphalt, noise barriers and treatment of stormwater - Work start expected as soon as possible from 2031
## Key facts Project: MeMe Section: A2 between Mendrisio and Melano Publication deadline: 13 October Promoting authority: Federal Roads Office (USTRA) Work start: from 2031 (optimistic scenario) Mentioned cost: 100 million francs
The Federal Roads Office (USTRA) has made official the publication of the design for the MeMe project, a comprehensive rehabilitation plan that concerns the section of the A2 motorway located between Mendrisio and Melano. The document can be consulted in the municipalities of Val Mara and Mendrisio until 13 October. The primary objective of the intervention is the acoustic rehabilitation of a section where the noise limit values are currently exceeded, particularly between the Lenaccio area and the Orto il gelso area.
### Technical details of the interventions
The plan foresees the use of sound-absorbing pavement and the adjustment of the existing noise barriers. To reduce acoustic impact, the existing protections will be raised by about 2 meters through the installation of glass walls. In addition to acoustic aspects, the MeMe project includes the construction of three new facilities for stormwater treatment, located respectively at the height of Sovaglia, next to the Lenaccio viaducts and in the Campaccio area.
The project does not only address noise and environment, but also intervenes on safety infrastructure. The adaptation of the emergency lane on the Lenaccio viaducts and the rehabilitation of the access ramps to the rest areas of Segoma are planned. These measures are described by USTRA as necessary to adapt the motorway section to the required standards, while ensuring a more efficient management of water and road safety in the affected section. ## Implications for cross-border commuting The stretch of A2 between Mendrisio and Melano represents a key axis for thousands of workers who cross the border each day to reach their workplaces in the Canton of Ticino. Any structural intervention on this segment directly affects the quality of life and traffic flow for those holding a G permit and traveling these roads. Although the goal is noise reduction, carrying out work of such magnitude inevitably involves a transition phase that cross-border workers will have to manage.
### Timing analysis and alternatives A critical fact emerges from the timelines communicated by USTRA: the works, in the best case, may begin from 2031. This means that for the coming years the current situation will remain unchanged. Moreover, the MeMe project is defined as a temporary measure. USTRA has in fact specified that the possibility of tunnelling the entire motorway segment in the future is not excluded, although such an operation would not occur before 2055.
For the cross‑border worker planning their movements, this means that the current sound‑recovery solution is the only concrete short‑ and medium‑term answer to prevent the population and those passing through from being exposed to noise levels above those specified by the OIF. The temporary nature of the project suggests that the infrastructure will continue to evolve, but the timeframe for more radical changes (such as the tunnel) is extremely far away.
### Criticisms and doubts about the project The project has already raised political questions. Councillor Andrea Rigamonti highlighted some criticisms through an inquiry, questioning the investment's effectiveness. In particular, it was asked what the State Council's position is regarding a plan that, despite an estimated cost of 100 million francs, would not guarantee compliance with noise limits at more than 40% of control points. This fact raises doubts about the real ability of the project to permanently solve the noise problem for those living and working along this road axis.

Although work is not expected to start before 2031, planning traffic flows during the adaptation of emergency lanes and the laying of sound‑absorbing asphalt will be crucial to avoid delays at the border crossings and along the A2.
What to do and how to monitor
Those interested in technical details or wishing to provide feedback on the project design can visit the municipalities of Val Mara and Mendrisio by the deadline of 13 October. This is the official public consultation window. After this phase, the project will move into subsequent technical planning and final approval stages before actual execution.
For cross‑border workers, attention will shift to mobility management. Ahead of future road works, it is advisable to assess the impact such interventions could have on travel times. item.title: Average salary in Como and Lombardy: 2024 data
item.description: In 2024 the average annual salary in Lombardy rises to 30,384.07 euros, but almost half of the workers do not exceed 25,000 euros.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2024 the employee base rises to 3,776,242 units with a 1.55% growth - The average annual salary is 30,384.07 euros with a 3.65% increase - Almost half of workers do not exceed the threshold of 25,000 euros per year
Employment growth: plus 1.55% compared to 2023 Average annual salary: 30,384.07 euros Nominal salary increase: plus 3.65% Workers under 20,000 euros: 1,380,567 units, equal to 36.56% of the total Workers under 25,000 euros: 49.66% of the overall base
The new report drawn up by UIL Lombardia, entitled Lombardy and Provinces - The value of work. Salaries, continuity and quality of work in 2024 and based on INPS Observatory data, highlights that despite a nominal growth in wages and employment, the Lombardy labor market continues to conceal deep inequalities and situations of marked precariousness. During 2024, the overall base of dependent workers belonging to the non-agricultural private sector rises to 3,776,242 units, recording an increase of 1.55% compared to the previous year. At the same time, the average annual salary reaches 30,384.07 euros, marking a 3.65% increase in nominal terms. However, this average figure tends to mask a much more complex and uneven internal reality for workers in general. Within the regional framework, in fact, as many as 1,380,567 workers, corresponding to 36.56% of the total base, fail to exceed the threshold of 20,000 gross euros per year. The situation appears even more critical if we consider that almost one worker in two, equal to 49.66% of the total, earns a total of less than 25,000 gross euros per year. As underlined by Antonio Albrizio, General Secretary of UIL Lombardia, the report confirms that the recorded economic growth must necessarily translate into a higher quality of work and a much more balanced distribution of the wealth produced. For the trade union organization, stable wages and good employment must remain at the center of regional policies to prevent economic expansion from leaving behind large segments of the working population. On the general economic front, the data highlight how the numerical progression of the employed does not automatically correspond to an improvement in real living conditions for all active employees in the Lombardy area, requiring a careful analysis of the contractual and salary dynamics that characterize the various provinces and various local economic sectors, with particular reference to the categories most exposed to economic vulnerability and contractual discontinuity during the twelve months of the reference year. ### Difficulties for young people and gender differences
The structural criticalities of the Lombard labour market particularly affect the most vulnerable groups, starting with the new generations and the female component. According to the report prepared on the basis of the findings of the INPS Observatory, over 1.38 million workers remain confined below the threshold of 20 thousand euros per year, and among young people up to 34 years of age this proportion widely exceeds 50%, specifically reaching 50.31% of employees under 35. Salvatore Monteduro, UIL Lombardy Confederal Secretary, highlights that the main problem is not only how many workers appear in official statistics, but how much income, continuity and autonomy can really produce the work offered by the regional economic system. Analyzing in detail the condition of young employees, who represent 33.22% of the total regional audience with about 1.25 million individuals, a picture of strong precariousness emerges: 50.31% do not exceed 20,000 euros per year and 65.18% remain permanently below 25,000 euros per year. In a region characterized by a particularly high cost of living, this persistent economic gap drastically limits the concrete possibility for young people to achieve effective housing and family autonomy, delaying emancipation and personal stability.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Sectoral analysis and necessary interventions
The strong economic polarization of the Lombardy labor market is confirmed by the wage gap between the various productive sectors, a disparity exceeding 54,000 euros per year among the economic activities considered. It ranges from an average of 67,750.86 euros recorded in the Finance and Insurance sector to a mere 13,215.45 euros found in the Accommodation and Food Service sector. In this very tourism and catering sector, economic precariousness assumes particularly significant dimensions, given that 76.20% of employees fail to reach the minimum threshold of 20,000 gross euros per year. Dario Esposito, Coordinator of UIL Lario, highlights how these regional data find particularly concerning confirmation in the Como area as well, where wages, which are on average lower than the Lombardy average, constantly contend with a steadily rising cost of living. In the Como area, work is not lacking, but too often it fails to guarantee sufficient income, contractual stability, and concrete opportunities to plan one's future, feeding a dangerous spiral of precariousness that specifically penalizes young people, women, and workers employed in the most fragile economic sectors. To reverse this negative trend, trade unions reiterate the need to intervene decisively on employment quality, strengthening national collective bargaining agreements, taking targeted action against involuntary part-time work, and promoting active policies to increase wages and job stability at the territorial level. To delve deeper into one's wage situation and accurately analyze the data relating to one's professional and social security classification, it is possible to check simulations and economic parameters using the online [calculator](nav:calculator).

In the detail of the document filed with the Grand Council, the State Council is asked to quantify the greater financial need linked to the individual reduction of premiums taking into account three different hypotheses of increase compared to the previous year: increases of 3%, 5% and 7%. For each of these three scenarios, MEPs call for a precise distinction between overall spending, funding from federal sources and the net burden that would actually remain with the Canton. The discussion on therapeutic cannabis in Canton Ticino involves representatives of CanMedTicino, led by president Gennaro Ausiello, who are preparing a new proposal following the recent halt received from the cantonal health authorities. The central theme concerns therapeutic continuity for patients who need these treatments, a topic officially addressed following the responses received on September 3 and 4 from the Cantonal Medical Officer, the Cantonal Pharmacist, and the Director of DSS, Raffaele De Rosa. The Cannabis Medica Ticino Association outlined its position in a note, highlighting how the health authorities recognized the practical difficulties related to the variability of cannabis inflorescences and shared the goal of ensuring continuity of care. ### The association's position and the authorities' response
Despite the halt received, Gennaro Ausiello, who lives with neurological disorders, chronic pain, and fatigue and has turned his patient experience into associative commitment, clearly stated that the association does not intend to give up. The formulated proposal was rejected, but the critical issues that prompted its development were officially recognized. From an operational standpoint, CanMedTicino points out that the responses received from the authorities do not indicate an operational alternative to the rejected model, nor a precise timeframe to identify one. The current situation highlights the gap between the clinical needs observed in the field by chronic patients and the limits imposed by the federal regulatory framework, which strictly regulates medical prescriptions and the distribution of cannabis-based therapies.

item.title: Living in Brenta and working in Ticino: the guide
item.description: Discover the pros and cons of living at Brenta and working in Ticino. Journey times, costs, advantages and taxation for border workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - New Cross-Border Worker Agreement in effect from January 1, 2024. - Tax exemption increased to CHF 10,000 for new cross-border workers. - Withholding tax is deducted in Switzerland, with tax credit in Italy.
## Key facts New Cross-Border Worker Agreement: January 1, 2024 Ratification Italy: Law 83 of 13/6/2023 Double Taxation Convention: December 9, 1976 Old Cross-Border Worker Exemption: CHF 7,500 (until 2033) New Cross-Border Worker Exemption: CHF 10,000 Swiss Withholding Tax: Deducted in Switzerland Italian Tax Credit: Section CE of the 730 form
Transferring residency to an Italian border municipality like Brenta, with the aim of working in Ticino, requires careful consideration of several factors, chief among them the impact of the new Cross-Border Worker Agreement, which came into effect on January 1, 2024. This agreement, signed on December 23, 2020, and ratified by Italy with Law 83 of June 13, 2023, introduces significant changes compared to the previous regulations. The Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland, dated December 9, 1976, continues to represent the reference regulatory framework, but the new agreement modifies some practical aspects for cross-border workers. One of the most relevant changes concerns the tax exemption: for the so-called «new» cross-border workers, meaning those who were not already active in Ticino before July 17, 2023, the threshold for exemption from Ticino cantonal tax has been raised to CHF 10,000. For «old» cross-border workers, who retain the right to the CHF 7,500 exemption, a transitional regime is foreseen which will extend until 2033. It is fundamental to understand that the withholding tax on employment income is deducted exclusively in Switzerland. Italy, to avoid double taxation, grants a tax credit, which cross-border workers can claim by completing section CE of the 730 form. This mechanism ensures that income earned in Switzerland is not taxed twice. The choice to reside in Brenta, as in other neighboring municipalities, is often dictated by the search for a potentially lower cost of living compared to Ticino, while maintaining geographical proximity that allows for manageable commute times. However, it is essential to analyze in detail transport costs, infrastructure, and tax specifics to make an informed decision. The goal is to balance the economic benefits derived from working in a high-income market like Ticino with daily needs and tax obligations in the country of residence. ### Implicazioni Fiscali e Previdenziali: Dettagli per il Frontaliere La gestione fiscale per chi vive a Brenta e lavora in Ticino è un aspetto cruciale, influenzato dal nuovo Accordo sui frontalieri. L'imposta alla fonte, prelevata direttamente dalla busta paga svizzera, si basa su aliquote che variano in funzione del reddito e dello stato civile. Per i contribuenti con un reddito annuo lordo fino a CHF 148'200, è applicata un'aliquota che tiene conto anche della deduzione per la franchigia (CHF 10'000 per i nuovi frontalieri, CHF 7'500 per i vecchi). Oltre a queste imposte dirette, i lavoratori dipendenti devono considerare i contributi sociali svizzeri. L'AVS/AI/IPG ammonta al 5.3% del salario lordo, a cui si aggiunge l'1.1% per AD/AC (fino al cap di CHF 148'200). La LAINF (assicurazione contro gli infortuni non professionali) varia tra lo 0.7% e l'1.5%, mentre la LPP (Cassa Pensione) ha aliquote progressive, a partire dal 7% per la fascia d'età 25-34 anni, fino a superare il 18% per le fasce più anziane, applicata sulla parte di salario eccedente il minimo LPP. Sul versante italiano, l'IRPEF prevede un'aliquota del 23% per scaglioni di reddito fino a €28'000, che sale al 35% per redditi tra €28'001 e €50'000, e al 43% per quelli superiori a €50'000. La convenzione contro le doppie imposizioni, tramite il credito d'imposta, evita che il reddito venga tassato due volte, ma è essenziale una corretta dichiarazione dei redditi in entrambi i paesi per ottimizzare il carico fiscale complessivo. Per quanto riguarda l'assicurazione malattia (LAMal), i frontalieri con permesso G hanno diritto di optare per l'assicurazione svizzera o quella italiana. Se si sceglie la LAMal, è possibile beneficiare di franchigie adulte che vanno da CHF 300 a CHF 2'500, con un impatto diretto sul premio mensile. La scelta tra le due opzioni assicurative dipenderà dalle esigenze personali, dalla composizione familiare e dai costi associati.

Although the source does not provide specific data on the cost of living in Brenta or exact travel times, it is common practice for neighboring Italian municipalities to offer economic attractiveness in terms of rents and property prices. However, this advantage must be weighed against the additional costs associated with commuting. The time spent reaching the workplace in Ticino, whether by private vehicle or public transport, directly affects the quality of life and operational costs (fuel, vehicle wear and tear, season tickets). Italian road infrastructure and border crossings, such as Brogeda, can present traffic issues, especially during peak hours, prolonging travel times. It is advisable to inquire about local traffic conditions and alternative routes, as well as available public transport options connecting Brenta to the main Ticino locations. item.title: Bally crisis in Caslano: another 25 dismissed in Ticino
item.description: New collective dismissal procedure for Bally in Caslano: another 25 administrative staff at risk. Financial data and the Transliq AG moratorium.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bally crisis: boutique closures and bankruptcies - Total shutdown of activities in Caslano - Another 25 laid off in administration - Red balances with millions in losses
Buyer fund: Regent LP Production site: Caslano Procedure company: Transliq AG Dismissals: 25 workers Current employees: 54 staff members 2024 Loss: 60.5 million 2025 Loss: 27.7 million
The trajectory of the historic luxury brand Bally has marked a new and dramatic chapter, marked by bankruptcy procedures, boutique closures, and failed attempts to sell the brand over the past two years. Ever since US investment fund Regent LP took over the company in August 2024, the situation has taken a complex turn culminating in the total shutdown of production activities at the Ticino site in Caslano. Concern among workers and former employees has reached extremely high levels following the latest official announcements.
### The new collective dismissal procedure
According to the latest reports from the newspaper laRegione, the company Transliq AG — tasked with managing the delicate phase of the composition moratorium — has announced a new collective dismissal procedure. This measure risks directly hitting another 25 administrative workers, in what many fear may not be the last round of cuts. The downsizing of the company's footprint in the region appears merciless in its numbers when looking at the recent evolution of the brand's workforce in Canton Ticino.
### The reduction of the workforce in Caslano
Originally, Bally employed 169 people across Switzerland, with as many as 122 employed right at the Caslano plant. Out of about 100 employees still present in June, the situation has further plummeted, dropping to just 54 staff members. Added to this figure is a dozen collaborators still active in the Swiss retail network. A drastically compromised employment picture that puts at risk historic professional skills tied to the Ticino region and local manufacturing tradition. The workforce downsizing and the production halt in Caslano represent a heavy blow to the local economic fabric and to the workers revolving around Canton Ticino. The evolution of the corporate crisis shows how fragile employment stability in the manufacturing and luxury sectors can be in the face of changes in ownership and complex financial management like that of the US fund Regent LP. For those who work or have worked at the plant, the debt-restructuring moratorium managed by Transliq AG opens a phase of extreme uncertainty, in which every single administrative and production job is called into question. ### Financial data and the collapse of the accounts To confirm the severity of the picture are the company's accounts recorded over the last three years. After a positive EBITDA of 43.5 million francs in 2023, 2024 marked a vertical collapse ending with a red of 60.5 million. In 2025 the loss partially reduced to 27.7 million, but the operating cash flow remained widely negative by 16.45 million francs. These numbers explain the speed with which the situation moved from relaunch attempts to the closure of production activities and personnel cuts. ### The sales plan and the future of the plant To attempt to save operations, a sales process for the production facility was launched within the framework of the moratorium. The operation aims at the transfer of the Caslano site, including plants, lease agreements, and employment contracts, with the primary objective of resuming production and protecting local jobs. Excluded from the negotiation, however, is the brand, which is fresh from two previous acquisition attempts that ended in nothing. This separation between the brand and the production infrastructures represents the last card left to preserve the Swiss structure and give a future to the remaining employees, pending the outcome of ongoing negotiations.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). The crisis affecting the Caslano plant requires careful reflection on the protection tools and guarantees available to workers involved in collective dismissal procedures and debt-restructuring moratoriums in Switzerland. When a company faces such a profound restructuring with the involvement of Transliq AG and a drastic reduction of the workforce from 122 to just 54 employees in Caslano, employees must carefully monitor every phase of bankruptcy proceedings and verify their contractual rights.
### Operational steps in case of restructurings and layoffs
Workers affected by collective dismissal measures must promptly liaise with the procedure's management bodies to verify back pay, liquidation conditions, and any protections provided by Swiss labor law. It is essential to gather all documentation relating to one's employment position, from contracts to the latest pay slips, keeping in mind that asset variations or job losses in Switzerland can also have repercussions on the management of any cross-border social security or tax positions.
### Support tools for crisis management
Faced with job loss in the Canton of Ticino, those in a professional transition phase must carefully evaluate the next steps to protect their economic stability. For a comprehensive analysis of one's income situation, employment prospects, and to navigate the available options in case of unemployment or relocation in the region, it is advisable to consult the in-depth analysis and financial planning tools dedicated to workers active in Swiss territory, checking the support services and employment opportunities available via [job listings](nav:jobs).

item.title: Living in Veniano and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide for those who live in Veniano and work in Canton Ticino: connections, tax at source, social security and aspects of the transfer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Veniano is located in the province of Como and is convenient for Ticino - Frontier workers pay withholding tax in Switzerland - Italy eliminates double taxation with a tax credit - The New Frontier Workers Agreement has been in force since January 1, 2024
## Key facts - Where: Veniano (Como), Italy - Work destination: Canton Ticino, Switzerland - Tax agreement: In force since January 1, 2024 - Relevant bodies: FTA, Italian Revenue Agency, INPS - Health insurance: LAMal option for frontier workers
Moving to Veniano for those who choose to work in Canton Ticino represents a strategic logistical solution for many commuting professionals. The geographical position in the Como area allows for a careful evaluation of road and highway connections to border crossings, facilitating daily travel to major Ticino economic centers such as Mendrisio, Lugano, and Chiasso. Analyzing travel times and road conditions is essential before planning a change of residence, taking into account the transient traffic that characterizes peak hours along the highway routes.
### Logistical aspects and road conditions from the Como area From the perspective of road connections, those residing in Veniano can easily access the highway network and provincial roads that lead quickly to the border customs posts. Daily commuting requires careful planning of departure times to optimize travel times and avoid the most intense congestion recorded near the main customs crossings during work shift changes. The proximity to customs transit points overall reduces logistical inconvenience compared to other more distant areas, making the Como municipality a particularly sought-after residential base for those who regularly cross the border for professional reasons.
The evaluation of the housing context in Veniano also includes the analysis of the local cost of living compared to salaries earned in Swiss francs. Although the Italian real estate market offers different opportunities compared to Ticino urban centers, it is necessary to carefully weigh fixed expenses related to home management, transportation, and primary services. Frontier workers must carefully consider how their net income is affected by tax and social security deductions applied across the border, comparing them with the purchasing power guaranteed in the Italian territory of residence. The regulatory and fiscal framework governing the status of frontier workers between Italy and Switzerland is governed by the New Agreement on Frontier Workers, which entered into force on 1 January 2024 after its signature on 23 December 2020 and Italian ratification with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. With regard to the taxation of income from employment, the tax at source is withheld directly in Switzerland, while Italy eliminates double taxation through the tax credit mechanism declared in the EC framework of model 730. This method guarantees a clear distribution of the tax levy between the two Contracting States, surpassing the old regimes and offering greater legal certainty to taxpayers.
### Differences between old and new frontier workers A fundamental discriminating element introduced by the legislation concerns the distinction between so-called old border workers, i.e. those who were already such before 17 July 2023, and new hires. For the former, there is a transitional regime that lasts from 2024 to 2033 with a specific exemption set at 7,500 euros, while for new border crossers the applicable exemption amounts to 10,000 euros. This distinction has a direct impact on the calculation of the total taxes due to the Italian Treasury and requires a careful verification of your previous contributory position before making any choice of employment or residence.
On the pension front
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). The management of health coverage is another crucial node for those who choose to settle in Veniano and maintain an occupation in Canton Ticino. Border workers classified with a G permit can exercise the right of option between the Swiss health system through LAMal and the Italian National Health Service. The choice must be weighed by evaluating the applicable deductibles for adults, which usually vary between 300 and 2,500 Swiss francs, and the related benefits guaranteed in the two systems. It is essential to respect the deadlines and formal procedures for communicating your decision to the competent bodies, avoiding penalties or insurance discoveries during the transition period.
### Operating procedure and calculation tools Before finalizing the transfer to Veniano and hiring in Ticino, it is advisable to use financial simulation tools to accurately estimate the overall economic impact on the paycheck and family budget. The use of special digital tools allows the net salary to be calculated transparently, taking into account cantonal and federal withholding taxes administered by the Federal Tax Administration (AFC/ESTV) and the provisions established by federal and cantonal laws. To deepen the economic planning and check all the updated salary parameters, it is advisable to consult the [calcolatore fiscale](nav:calculator)

item.title: Living in Veleso and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Practical guide for those who wish to reside in Veleso and commute in Ticino: taxation, permits and management of the cost of living.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Imposta alla fonte trattenuta solo in Svizzera - Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri in vigore dal 1° gennaio 2024 - Franchigia di 10.000 euro per i nuovi frontalieri - Esenzione di 7.500 euro per i vecchi frontalieri
## Fatti chiave Accordo Frontalieri: firmato 23/12/2020, in vigore 01/01/2024 Ratifica Italia: Legge 83 del 13/06/2023 Convenzione doppie imposizioni: 09/12/1976 Franchigia nuovi frontalieri: 10.000 euro Esenzione vecchi frontalieri: 7.500 euro
Il trasferimento a Veleso per chi lavora nel Canton Ticino richiede l'analisi di precise norme fiscali e amministrative. Il quadro normativo attuale è definito dal Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri, firmato il 23 dicembre 2020 ed entrato in vigore il 1° gennaio 2024, dopo la ratifica italiana avvenuta con la Legge 83 del 13 giugno 2023. Questo accordo ridefinisce i parametri di tassazione per chi risiede in Italia e lavora in Svizzera.
### La struttura fiscale per il residente a Veleso Per un lavoratore che risiede a Veleso, l'imposta alla fonte sul reddito da lavoro viene trattenuta esclusivamente in Svizzera. L'Italia evita la doppia imposizione attraverso l'applicazione di un credito d'imposta, che viene gestito nel quadro CE della dichiarazione dei redditi 730. Questo meccanismo è coerente con la Convenzione per l'eliminazione delle doppie imposizioni firmata tra Italia e Svizzera il 9 dicembre 1976.
L'amministrazione di tali imposte è affidata all'Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni (AFC/ESTV) a livello federale e alle rispettive amministrazioni cantonali. È importante sottolineare che enti come l'Ufficio Federale di Statistica (BFS) o l'Ufficio Federale delle Assicurazioni Sociali (UFAS) non hanno competenza nella fissazione delle aliquote fiscali, ma si occupano rispettivamente di rilevazioni statistiche e previdenza sociale. Il frontaliere che sceglie Veleso come dimora deve quindi coordinare i propri obblighi tra l'AFC svizzera e l'Agenzia delle Entrate italiana per l'ottimizzazione del credito d'imposta. ## Analisi pratica e scenari
La scelta di vivere a Veleso comporta l'applicazione di regimi fiscali differenti a seconda della data di inizio dell'attività di frontaliere. I cosiddetti 'vecchi frontalieri', ovvero coloro che possedevano già tale status prima del 17 luglio 2023, beneficiano di un regime transitorio che copre il periodo 2024–2033, con un'esenzione di 7.500 euro. Al contrario, i 'nuovi frontalieri' possono usufruire di una franchigia di 10.000 euro.
### Impatto sulle trattenute e previdenza Il salario percepito in Ticino è soggetto a diverse trattenute previdenziali obbligatorie. I contributi AVS/AI/IPG ammontano al 5.3% a carico del dipendente, mentre l'assicurazione disoccupazione (AD/AC) incide per l'1.1%, con un tetto massimo di 148.200 CHF. La previdenza professionale (LPP) varia tra il 7% e il 18% a seconda della fascia d'età, partendo dai 25 anni, mentre la LAINF oscilla tra lo 0.7% e l'1.5%.
Per quanto riguarda la salute, i frontalieri con permesso G hanno diritto d'opzione per l'assicurazione malattia LAMal. Le franchigie per gli adulti variano da 300 a 2.500 CHF. Questo sistema permette di gestire la copertura sanitaria in modo flessibile, a seconda delle necessità individuali e della preferenza tra il sistema svizzero o quello italiano.
### Confronto con la fiscalità italiana Il reddito prodotto in Svizzera, una volta detratte le imposte alla fonte, deve essere confrontato con le aliquote IRPEF italiane per l'eventuale integrazione o per il calcolo del credito d'imposta. Le aliquote attuali prevedono il 23% fino a 28.000 euro, il 35% tra 28.001 e 50.000 euro, e il 43% per le quote eccedenti i 50.000 euro. Un frontaliere che risiede a Veleso deve quindi monitorare costantemente il proprio reddito complessivo per evitare sorprese in fase di dichiarazione dei redditi, utilizzando strumenti di [calcolo fiscale](nav:calculator) per simulare il netto reale.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ## Guida all'azione per il trasferimento
Chi decide di trasferirsi a Veleso per lavorare in Ticino deve seguire una procedura precisa per regolarizzare la propria posizione amministrativa e fiscale. Il primo passo è l'ottenimento del permesso G, che attesta lo status di frontaliere e permette l'accesso ai diritti d'opzione per la LAMal e l'applicazione del regime fiscale di frontiera.
### Step operativi per il frontaliere 1. Richiesta del Permesso G: l'istanza va presentata alle autorità competenti del Canton Ticino per formalizzare il rapporto di lavoro transfrontaliero. 2. Scelta dell'assicurazione sanitaria: decidere se aderire alla LAMal svizzera (scegliendo la franchigia tra 300 e 2.500 CHF) o mantenere la copertura italiana. Per approfondire i costi, è possibile consultare la guida su [LAMal e CMI](nav:health). 3. Configurazione previdenziale: verificare che i contributi AVS e LPP siano correttamente versati in busta paga secondo le fasce d'età previste. 4. Gestione fiscale: in occasione della dichiarazione dei redditi in Italia, inserire i dati del reddito svizzero nel quadro CE del modello 730 per richiedere il credito d'imposta e neutralizzare la doppia imposizione.
### Considerazioni logistiche e costi Il pendolarismo da Veleso verso i centri produttivi ticinesi richiede una pianificazione dei tempi di percorrenza e dei costi di trasporto. È consigliabile valutare l'impatto delle spese di viaggio sul salario netto, considerando l'uso dell'auto e l'eventuale acquisto della vignetta autostradale. Per un confronto dettagliato tra le spese di residenza in Italia e i costi della vita in Svizzera, si suggerisce di utilizzare il comparatore sul [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living).
Per calcolare con precisione l'impatto delle trattenute AVS, LPP e dell'imposta alla fonte sul proprio stipendio lordo, il consiglio è di utilizzare il nostro [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).
